Title: The haze demands more than another Asean pledge
Article:
AS the Air Pollutant Index for Kuching inched into hazardous territory last week and remains in the unhealthy category this week, alarm bells are ringing as a state of  emergency was declared yesterday.
The city is completely smothered in a mood-depressing smog as  forest fires raged uncontrollably in much of Indonesia's Kalimantan, producing the toxic haze that spread across the border into Sarawak.
Social media lit up with rankings of most polluted global cities as a trending topic,  some pointing to Kuching overtaking Delhi, India,  right at the top.
What is perhaps even more depressing is the limited options to tackle the problem, even as Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto visited the sites of some of the worst fires to lend  urgency in fighting them.
As it happens, reports now point to the haze spreading as far away as Manila in the Philippines.
Four of the five original members of Asean — Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore and the Philippines — are now mired in unhealthy air quality.
Amid all this, Sarawak Yang di-Pertua Negeri Tun Wan Junaidi Tuanku Jaafar offered some well-meaning ideas to address what has become a region-wide issue of crisis proportions.
He dismissed the reflexive urge to indulge in any blame game.
Wan Junaidi recalled travelling to Jakarta in 2015 as then natural resources and environment minister during another severe haze crisis, offering Malaysia's assistance to  fight  forest fires, including use of our amphibious Bombardier aircraft.
Indonesia  accepted Malaysia's offer,  even though Wan Junaidi acknowledged the particular difficulty of accessing the remote interior of Borneo where fires raged.
The Sarawak head of state believes it is time to add teeth to the Asean Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution (AATHP) signed in 2002.
"We should look at new technologies and methods to fight forest fires."
Wan Junaidi also suggests the pooling of resources within Asean.
"Imagine if every Asean country has two Bombardier aircraft. We will have 20 planes to scoop water and dump over the burning areas."
It is becoming plainly obvious that half the members of Asean (Brunei, wedged between Sarawak and Sabah, is also experiencing the ill-effects of the haze) are in this together right now.
The AATHP must be quickly activated and faster decision-making mechanisms in place so fires can be fought almost as soon as they appear.
Since forest fires are almost a yearly phenomenon, the fire-fighting response must be readied early in anticipation of them getting out of control.
To be sure, there is no substitute for taking preventive action to avoid having fires spreading out of control in the first place.
Perhaps regional collaboration to address haze pollution should include devising an early-warning system for forest fire prevention?
Other countries outside Asean are beginning to come forward with offers of assistance to fight the fires.
The Asean Secretariat should coordinate with countries within and outside Asean and Indonesia so any assistance offered is swiftly and efficiently rolled out.
The tens of millions of human lives and even wildlife adversely  affected by this latest round of haze pollution in Borneo and beyond cannot simply wait for the fires to run their course, wreaking untold damage in the process.
The writer views developments in the nation, region and the wider world from his vantage point in Kuching

Title: Puspakom eyes 24-hour operations from January
Article:
KLANG: The Computerised Vehicle Inspection Centre (Puspakom) plans to operate 24 hours a day from next January to provide greater convenience to the public for vehicle inspections.
Puspakom chief executive officer Mahmood Razak Bahman said the plan would depend on public response to the extension of operating hours to seven days a week from November, as well as the availability of sufficient manpower.
"We have engaged with the National Union of Commercial Workers (NUCW) and the Puspakom Staff Union to gauge their views on a concept that provides more reasonable working hours, specifically eight to 10 hours a day compared with the current 12 hours, as well as two rest days a week instead of 1.
"As for 24-hour operations, the target is to launch them next January, subject to public response to the seven-day operation, workforce readiness and operational capacity," he told Bernama after launching the GiCheck Auto Weekend 2026 event at the Aeon Bukit Tinggi premises here today.
Also present were Transport Ministry Land Division secretary Datuk Mohamed Irwan Mansor and Puspakom chief operating officer Dr Ahmad Zahiri Ismail.
Meanwhile, Mahmood said Puspakom was introducing several other initiatives, including a new "community hero" recognition award and expanded on-site inspection services for customers.
He said the initiatives included the Puspakom Towering Malaysian Awards and enhanced on-site inspection services to make the inspection process more convenient for vehicle owners.
"The new award programme is created specifically to honour individuals who bring about positive change to society or the environment, even though their contributions often go unnoticed by the general public.
"This recognition initiative is currently being developed in collaboration with strategic partners and selected media agencies, with further details to be announced soon," he said.
Elaborating, he said the modernisation initiative was supported by various interactive activities, including GiCheck Auto Weekend 2026, aimed at delivering road safety messages to the public through hands-on and practical engagement.
He said the measures were expected to improve Puspakom's overall operational efficiency while strengthening ties between the vehicle inspection agency and the local community.
The inaugural GiCheck Auto Weekend 2026 featured various technical demonstrations, including a "Driving Under the Influence" (DUI) simulation, a "seat belt convincer" test and an exhibition of Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) technology.
Held in conjunction with the National Month celebrations, the event carried the theme "Driving Safer Roads Together".
"Through GiCheck Auto Weekend, we aim to make road safety education more accessible, engaging and relevant to Malaysians, while raising public awareness of the vital role vehicle inspections play in keeping our roads safe," he said.

Title: Two more survivors, including Chinese national, rescued 10 days after devastating Nepal floods
Article:
KATHMANDU: A Chinese national was pulled alive from a tunnel in Nepal on Saturday, authorities said, 10 days after a wall of ice, rock and mud tore through a Himalayan valley, killing more than 1,300 people.
The Nepali army said Lu Haitao was rescued from inside a 225-metre tunnel at the Upper Trishuli-1 Hydropower Project.
He was the third person to be pulled alive from various tunnels where authorities believe about 900 people could be trapped following the Aug 26 collapse of a glacier on the upper reaches of the river.
On Friday, rescue workers pulled two people from another tunnel at the Upper Trishuli 3A Hydropower Station on the same river.
Authorities said Lu had no visible injuries and his vital signs were stable, but he showed signs of mild hypothermia.
Footage shared by the Nepali army showed him receiving emergency medical attention inside a helicopter that took him to an army hospital.
He appeared exhausted and disoriented, with dried mud and dust covering his skin and clothing. A uniformed medic carrying a stethoscope was seen checking him.
At least 1,344 people have been killed in Nepal in floods that swept away houses, roads and schools in towns and villages near the border with China's Tibet, the disaster management authority said on Friday. About 4,887 people remain missing, including 583 foreigners, many of them pilgrims and trekkers.
As of Sept 4, China said the death toll in Tibet stood at 31, with 531 others listed as missing, according to state media Xinhua.
A woman, Chandika Kumari Shrestha, was also rescued from her home in Betrawati on Saturday, the Nepali army said.
In an image shared by authorities, she was seen caked in mud inside a flooded underground structure as rescuers offered her water while working in a confined space filled with thick sludge.
At the Maithili Barrack in Nepal's Nuwakot district, families covered walls with posters showing loved ones believed to be trapped in the tunnels.
Among them was an image of Ishwor Poudel, the brother of 34-year-old Krishna Poudel.
Ishwor has worked in the tunnel of the Hakubesi Hydroelectric Project for the past three years.
Krishna said he last heard from his brother on Aug 26, shortly after floodwaters tore through the valley.
"I spoke to him at 7.30 am. before he went into the tunnel for work. Around 11.30am, after the floods came down, I finally got through and he told me: 'I'm trapped inside the tunnel.'"
The family has had no contact with him since, but remains hopeful. Survivors who escaped from the same tunnel told them that Ishwor was still alive.
"I met so many people who were able to escape and knew my brother. They told me,'Your brother is inside the tunnel, he was driving a vehicle inside.'
"They said they could hear the voices of about 200 to 300 people shouting from inside."

Title: Iraqis queue for fuel as regional war disrupts imports
Article:
BAGHDAD: Drivers formed long lines outside fuel stations in Baghdad on Saturday as gasoline supplies dropped in oil-rich Iraq due to import disruptions caused by the Middle East war.
Despite being OPEC's second largest oil producer, Iraq imports oil derivatives because its refineries do not produce enough gasoline to meet domestic demand.
In recent weeks, as regional hostilities drag on, long queues have been reappearing every few days, mostly outside government-run fuel stations in Baghdad and other provinces.
Baghdad resident Ibrahim Hashem waited for two hours outside a fuel station on Friday without any luck, only to return early the next day hoping to fill his car.
"It is unreasonable that we produce so many barrels of oil a day, yet still do not have enough gasoline to meet our daily needs," Hashem told AFP outside a fuel station in central Baghdad.
"We already suffer from traffic congestion because of the roads and lack of services. Now, it has become worse due to the gasoline shortage," he added.
Iraq's average daily consumption of gasoline is 33 million litres, but demand rises to 38 million when people panic over shortages, according to authorities.
The oil ministry said Friday that "regional events and the ongoing conflict are causing logistical challenges to tanker traffic, delaying their arrival at Iraqi ports."
It urged citizens to buy only the quantities they need and avoid crowding fuel stations for small amounts of gasoline.
Oil Minister Bassem Mohammed Khudair said on Friday that his ministry was addressing the "temporary shortage of gasoline" and that new shipments will arrive soon to help stabilise supplies.
Like other oil producers, Iraq has been greatly affected by the US-Iran conflict, which has choked off the strategic Strait of Hormuz.
Iraq is hugely dependent on oil exports, which make up about 90 percent of its budget revenues.
Before the war erupted in February, Iraq produced around four million barrels per day, and exported an average of 3.4 million bpd, mostly via Hormuz.
After a significant drop, Iraqi oil exports recovered  to more than 2.2 million bpd in August, according to the oil ministry.
Last month, Iran's state news agency IRNA said that over the past six months, Tehran has granted permission to "a number of Iraqi oil tankers" to pass through Hormuz.

Title: Philippine VP Duterte posts bail over 'grave threats' against president
Article:
MANILA: Philippine vice president Sara Duterte posted bail at a Manila courthouse on Saturday, a day after an arrest warrant was issued over her alleged death threat against the country's president.
Duterte was charged last month with "grave threats" stemming from a late-night news briefing in which she claimed to have hired a hitman to kill President Ferdinand Marcos, his wife and a congressman cousin should she be cut down first.
She later said the comments had been misconstrued.
The alleged assassination threat also forms a crucial element of her ongoing Senate impeachment trial, where a guilty verdict would see her removed from office and permanently banned from politics.
"The vice president voluntarily appeared before the court that issued the warrant, so there was no need for her to be arrested," her lawyer Lawrence Lim said.
He was speaking after Duterte emerged from the courthouse holding a court order confirming she had posted a cash bond totalling 360,000 pesos ($5,740).
She also underwent a standard booking procedure in which her fingerprints were recorded, though no mugshots were taken, Lim said.
Duterte said in a statement that her lawyers advised her to post bail for her safety.
"They explained to me that I would have better protection from civilians who would be able to monitor my situation, rather than being in detention where I would be isolated and have little protection," she said.
Prior to entering the courthouse, Duterte told reporters she feared for her life.
"I don't want to (post bail) if no one is watching," she said, claiming to be the victim of police harassment.
"Will they throw me into the (jail) and then one night I die in my sleep?" she said.
'GRAVE THREATS'
The Philippine presidential palace rejected Duterte's comments as "unfounded", saying police were merely implementing their mandate to protect Filipinos.
"This administration will never allow the police to be used to commit any form of violence," it said.
Under the Philippine legal code, a criminal conviction on the "grave threats" charge could carry a jail term of up to six months.
The vice president's legal team issued a statement on Friday saying she had "no intention of evading the law and will continue to exercise all her legal remedies."
Justice department officials have rejected her lawyers' argument that the vice president cannot be prosecuted for offences that are also tied to her impeachment.
Duterte was impeached in May by the House of Representatives, the lower chamber of parliament, on charges that also included graft and corruption.
A guilty verdict in the Senate – where her trial recently concluded its ninth week – would spell an end to a planned run for president in 2028.
Duterte first announced her candidacy in February.

Title: Sultan Nazrin: Cancer screening must reach every Malaysian
Article:
PETALING JAYA: Sultan of Perak Sultan Nazrin Muizzuddin Shah has called for greater emphasis on early cancer detection, stressing that access to health screening should be available to all Malaysians regardless of their social or economic background.
In his address at the launch of the National Cancer Congress Malaysia 2026 today, the ruler said a national screening programme should reach everyone, describing it as an important investment in the nation's wellbeing.
"Hope must also live in early detection more broadly. A national screening programme that reaches a plantation worker as easily as a company executive is not a luxury but one of the best investments we can make in the wellbeing of our people.
"I hope our health authorities, our insurers, our employers and every Malaysian family will come to see screening as an act of love, for ourselves and for those who depend on us."
On the congress, Sultan Nazrin outlined three priorities, calling for stronger research, evidence-based policymaking and greater public awareness of cancer.
"First, that our scientists and doctors continue research that is useful as well as rigorous, reaching patients in every state, not only our biggest cities.
"Second, that our policymakers listen closely to the evidence and the personal stories shared here and carry them into our national cancer strategy.
"Third, that each of us remembers that fighting cancer begins with our own choices, our own workplaces, and our willingness to talk openly about a disease too often discussed in hushed whispers."
Sultan Nazrin said no single hospital, ministry, university or congress could defeat cancer alone, stressing that progress required collective action.
He cited the partnership between the National Cancer Society of Malaysia and Sunway University as an example of the collaboration Malaysia needed to move the fight against cancer forward.
"There was a time when a cancer diagnosis was spoken of only in whispers, almost a final sentence rather than something that could be faced, and overcome.
"I am glad to say this is changing. Survival rates for many cancers have improved enormously within a single generation and Malaysian researchers and institutions are contributing real, original science to this progress, not simply borrowing it from elsewhere."
Also present were Sunway Group founder and chairman Tan Sri Jeffrey Cheah, National Cancer Society Malaysia president Datuk Dr Saunthari Somasundaram and Health Ministry deputy director-general (public health) Dr Ismuni Bohari.

Title: NKVE collapse: RSEA wants safety audit of highway structures
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Road Safety Expert Association (RSEA) has called for an immediate structural safety audit of potentially hazardous structures along Malaysia's major expressways following the collapse of a large structure onto the New Klang Valley Expressway (NKVE) near Shah Alam last night.
RSEA founder and road safety and motorsports adviser Jamil Manan Supri said the incident raised a critical road safety issue, stressing that structures located beside or above high-speed traffic must remain structurally sound throughout their service life.
"A structural failure on an expressway is not simply an infrastructure or traffic management problem. It has the potential to become a mass-casualty road safety hazard, particularly when motorists travelling at high speed have only seconds to detect and respond to an unexpected obstruction.
"RSEA therefore calls for an immediate structural safety audit of all large billboards, advertising structures, gantries and other potentially hazardous structures located along major expressways, with priority given to those positioned above, immediately beside or within the potential fall zone of live traffic," he said in a statement.
Jamil said the inspection must go beyond visual checks and include assessments of foundations, anchoring systems, bolts, welds and supporting frames, as well as corrosion, structural fatigue, deformation, vibration and wind-loading capacity.
"Every structure should be subject to mandatory periodic inspection and certification by competent and appropriately qualified professionals, with additional inspections following severe weather, vehicle impact or other abnormal events," he said.
He said the location of billboards must also be assessed from a road-user safety perspective, rather than solely for commercial visibility.
"Before a billboard or large advertising structure is approved, authorities should assess its potential fall zone and determine whether its failure could block multiple lanes, obstruct sight distance, interfere with traffic signs or create a serious hazard to motorists, particularly vulnerable road users such as motorcyclists.
"At the same time, the increasing use of illuminated and digital billboards requires stronger controls. Billboard lighting must not become a source of driver distraction or glare.
"Brightness, flashing, animation, rapid image changes, colour contrast, operating hours and positioning within the driver's field of vision should be regulated to ensure that advertising does not compete with traffic signs, signals, emergency warnings or other critical road information."
Jamil said RSEA also proposed the establishment of a National Highway Advertising and Structural Safety Register, clearly identifying the owner, designer, installer, approval status, structural certification, inspection history, maintenance records and next inspection date for every high-risk structure.
"This incident should therefore serve as a warning to all relevant authorities, highway operators, billboard owners and advertisers. Safety cannot be treated as a one-time approval requirement. It must be continuously managed throughout the entire lifecycle of the structure," he said.
Last night, all
northbound lanes of the NKVE
near Shah Alam were blocked, bringing traffic to a standstill shortly before midnight.
Photographs and video from the scene showed what appeared to be a large overhead highway gantry lying across the carriageway, with several heavy vehicles, including lorries, nearby.

Title: Sarawak remains worst hit as six areas record very unhealthy air quality
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Six areas in Sarawak recorded very unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 6pm, with the state remaining the worst affected by the haze.
Data published on the Department of Environment's Facebook page showed that 25 of 68 monitoring stations nationwide recorded unhealthy air quality, while another six recorded very unhealthy readings.
Kuching recorded the country's highest API reading at 275, followed by Sri Aman at 235, Serian at 230, Samarahan at 210, Bintulu at 209 and Samalaju at 208.
Under the API classification, readings above 200 are categorised as very unhealthy.
Stations recording unhealthy air quality included ILP Miri (191), Mukah (190), Miri (184), Sarikei (180), Sibu (176), Kimanis (171) and Labuan (170).
Other locations reporting unhealthy air quality included Limbang (163), Johan Setia (161), Bukit Rambai (159), Tangkak (158), Kota Kinabalu (158), Kluang (156), Nilai and Segamat (157 each), Seremban and Alor Gajah (155 each), as well as Putrajaya (151).
The data also showed that 26 stations recorded moderate air quality, while 10 recorded good air quality. No station recorded a hazardous API reading.
The API measures air quality based on pollutants including particulate matter. Readings from 101 to 200 are classified as unhealthy, while those exceeding 200 are categorised as very unhealthy.
The distribution map showed poorer air quality concentrated mainly in parts of Sarawak, while several areas in Peninsular Malaysia and Sabah also recorded unhealthy readings.

Title: Immigration steps up hunt for foreigners issued fraudulent PLKS
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Immigration Department will intensify enforcement operations to track down foreigners holding more than 1,300 Temporary Employment Visit Passes (PLKS) believed to have been irregularly approved through a syndicate uncovered under Op Crack.
Immigration Department director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said the department's enforcement division was also gathering intelligence on the ground to identify and locate foreigners holding the improperly approved passes.
"We will continue carrying out enforcement operations to trace the holders of PLKS that were approved irregularly.
"There are at least 1,300 of these PLKS which are believed to be in the hands of foreigners after being issued through the syndicate.
"We will either catch them through intelligence gathered or through targeted operations," he told the New Straits Times.
Zakaria said the department also welcomed information from the public that could assist enforcement officers in locating foreigners holding the irregularly approved PLKS.
He said information received would help the department identify and track down those who had benefited from the syndicate's activities.
"Rest assured that the identities of those who come forward with information would be kept strictly confidential," he said.
It was previously reported that immigration officers attempting to track down holders of the irregularly issued PLKS hit a snag after finding that their
registered addresses were also fake
.
The department conducted several raids at addresses linked to the affected permits as part of ongoing investigations.
However, officers found that the information registered under the permits did not correspond with the actual locations.
Zakaria said then that although their system contained certain addresses, officers found different premises when they visited the locations, while the employer information also did not match.
The department had earlier said it would
cancel all improperly approved PLKS
and trace their holders following the dismantling of a syndicate suspected of hacking the Malaysian Immigration System (MyIMMs) to manipulate the pass approval process.
Zakaria had said the move was the first step following the discovery of PLKS approvals that did not comply with procedures during Op Crack, a joint operation between the Immigration Department and the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC).
It was previously reported that
12 individuals
, including six Immigration Department personnel and a police officer, were detained by the MACC for allegedly being involved in the syndicate.
Investigations found that 1,306 PLKS were allegedly approved through unused foreign-worker quotas, resulting in an estimated RM2.4 million in lost levy payments.
Nine bank accounts containing about RM300,000 were also reportedly frozen as part of the investigation.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Indonesia rescues second orangutan mother and baby from wildfire
Article:
JAKARTA: An orangutan mother and her baby, threatened by encroaching wildfires to their habitat in Indonesia, were rescued earlier this week, authorities said in a statement Saturday.
The vast Southeast Asian archipelago has for weeks been fighting wildfires blanketing parts of Borneo and Sumatra with smog, with haze also contributing to air pollution in Malaysia, Singapore, and the Philippines.
The orangutan pair had been under observation since July after being spotted in a plantation area near a forest in West Kalimantan, a local natural resources conservation agency said in a statement.
But authorities decided to evacuate them to a rescue center managed by the wildlife foundation Yayasan Inisiasi Alam Rehabilitasi Indonesia (YIARI) on Thursday as fire spread near their habitat.
Their health is being closely monitored by veterinarians, but a preliminary check found no burn injuries on the two great apes.
"Exposure to smoke over a period of time... can affect the orangutan's respiratory system, especially when smoke concentrations in the habitat are very high," YIARI's veterinarian Komara, who like many Indonesians uses only one name, said in a statement.
"Both individuals will continue to be monitored while they are at the rescue and rehabilitation center."
The latest rescue means nine orangutans have been evacuated because of threats from wildfires in less than a month in the Ketapang district of West Kalimantan province, YIARI operational director Argitoe Ranting said.
"This shows that fires not only destroy forests but also deprive animals of shelter and food," Argitoe said.
Most animals "do not have many options" to relocate as their habitat burns, he added.
One orangutan died after being rescued last week, with a necropsy result pointing to smoke exposure as the cause of death, the West Kalimantan natural resources conservation agency said in a statement.

Title: Air we breathe could be harming children, says Sultan Nazrin
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Chemical emissions from industries, vehicle exhaust fumes, as well as water and soil pollution can no longer be regarded solely as environmental issues, as prolonged exposure has been linked to various cancers, including among children.
Sultan of Perak Sultan Nazrin Muizzuddin Shah said cancer prevention efforts should not focus solely on factors such as smoking and diet, but also address chemicals released by factories, vehicle emissions and other pollutants children may inhale or be exposed to daily.
He said the issue represented a gap that was not discussed often enough, despite the potential harm caused by environmental exposure.
"It sits in the shadows behind many of the cancer cases that fill our hospitals: the air our children breathe and the harm that too often is caused by what is hidden within it."
Sultan Nazrin said this at the launch of the National Cancer Congress Malaysia 2026 and the coffee table book, A Breath For The Future: Malaysia's National Lung Health Initiative.
He said the concern was particularly pertinent given the difficult environmental conditions affecting the region, including forest fires in Kalimantan, a dry season intensified by El Nino and winds blowing in an unfavourable direction for Malaysia.
He also urged Malaysia to take note of the emergence of so-called "cancer alleys", where heavy industry had grown faster than safeguards intended to protect nearby communities.
Citing communities in Louisiana in the United States, industrial areas in South Africa and China, and the Niger Delta in West Africa, where concerns had emerged over cancer risks associated with industrial activity and pollution, he said Malaysia should regard such examples as a warning.
"This is not a problem unique to any one country or industry and it is a pattern we in Malaysia, with our own industrial corridors and our own rivers running past factories and plantations, would be wise to take as a caution rather than a distant headline."
Sultan Nazrin also highlighted a documentary about a community in southern Iraq living near intensive oil and gas extraction, where routine gas flaring exposed residents to potentially harmful chemicals and children reportedly experienced unusually high rates of leukaemia.
He said the example illustrated the broader health risks posed by pollution, noting that scientists had learned over many years that pollution did not only harm the lungs.
"Chemicals released by industry, by traffic and by the fuels we burn to run both have been linked to childhood leukaemia and to cancers of the lung, the bladder and the breast in adults exposed over many years.
"Polluted water and soil bring their own dangers too, linked to cancers of the liver and digestive system downstream of poorly regulated factories.
"So when we talk about preventing cancer, we cannot speak only of smoking and diet, important as those are.
"We must also speak honestly about what our factories release, what our vehicles put into our streets and what we allow to settle into the lungs of a sleeping child."
Sultan Nazrin said Malaysia must therefore consider how it balances economic growth with environmental safeguards.
Pointing to London as an example, he said stronger environmental regulation could produce measurable improvements in public health.
Following the introduction of its Ultra Low Emission Zone, which charges the most polluting vehicles high fees to enter the city centre, children in central London
experienced significant improvements in lung function as toxic vehicle emissions fell.
"Before the scheme began, children in central London had noticeably weaker lungs than children in Luton, a town near London.
"Within five years, as toxic exhaust fell sharply in London, those children's lungs recovered so well that they nearly caught up with children in Luton.
"The number of London children with poorly functioning lungs fell from about one in seven to about one in 11.
"Damage many once thought was simply the price of city life turned out not to be permanent.
"Clean the air, and children's bodies can heal."
Sultan Nazrin said the lesson from London was a hopeful one.
"Pollution and disease are not simply facts of modern life we must accept. They are the result of choices, and choices can be changed.
"If a city as large as London can restore its children's lungs within five years, then Malaysia, blessed with rainforest, coastline and industries still young enough to build cleanly from the start, can protect the lungs and the futures of our own children."
He said addressing the issue was not a task for the Health Ministry alone, but required action across the environmental, transport and industrial sectors.
"It belongs equally to those responsible for our environment, our transport, our industry and business leaders, who must help weigh the cost of cleaner production against a cost that cannot be priced: a child's life.
"I say this not to single out any one sector, but because I believe Malaysia's industries, given the chance to lead on this, will find that cleaner growth and competitive growth need not be different things."
Present were Sunway Group founder and chairman Tan Sri Jeffrey Cheah, National Cancer Society Malaysia president Datuk Dr Saunthari Somasundaram and Health Ministry deputy director-general (public health) Dr Ismuni Bohari.

Title: Orange suits out, double standards must too, says criminologist
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission's (MACC) decision to stop requiring suspects to wear its orange uniform during remand proceedings is appropriate, but the policy must be applied equally regardless of a person's status, wealth or political position, said a criminologist.
Dr Haezreena Begum Abdul Hamid said the key issue was ensuring that investigation and punishment remained distinct, as a person brought before a court for remand was still a suspect and had not been found guilty.
"I think the main point here is that we need to separate investigation from punishment. When someone is brought to court for remand, that person is still a suspect. The court is not deciding guilt at that stage.
"So, in that sense, removing the orange uniform is appropriate. My only concern is that the policy must be clear and applied consistently," she told the New Straits Times.
Haezreena said allowing suspects to appear in civilian clothing could also reinforce the presumption of innocence, particularly given the strong visual association between the orange uniform and criminality.
"The problem with the orange uniform is that once you see someone wearing it, particularly in a photograph, you immediately associate that person with criminality.
"But this person may only be under investigation. So civilian clothing better reflects where they actually are in the criminal justice process."
However, she cautioned that the move could undermine public confidence if there appeared to be different standards for ordinary suspects and prominent individuals.
"In my opinion, the bigger issue is not really the orange uniform. It is whether everybody is treated the same.
"If an ordinary person is brought to court in orange and handcuffs, but a politician or prominent
businessman comes in civilian clothes without restraints, naturally people are going to question this double standard.
"That is where public confidence can be affected," she said.
Haezreena said MACC should introduce a clear written policy governing clothing and the use of restraints, with any differences in treatment based solely on objective considerations.
"If there is a reason for different treatment — security, escape risk or some operational concern — then there should be an objective reason for it.
"Status, wealth or political position should have nothing to do with it," she said.
She said the previous practice of suspects appearing publicly in distinctive orange clothing could also have lasting reputational and psychological consequences, even if they were subsequently not charged or were acquitted.
"Once someone's photograph in that orange uniform is everywhere, that image stays with them even if they are eventually not charged or are acquitted.
"From a criminological perspective, there is also labelling theory. Once society starts seeing you as a criminal, that label can follow you into your work, family and social life even if you are never convicted," she said.
Haezreena said the change could also affect media coverage of corruption cases, as images of suspects in orange uniforms could sometimes overshadow the substance of court proceedings.
"Civilian clothing may reduce that visual impression of guilt and hopefully shift the attention back to the investigation and the court proceedings," she said.
On the use of handcuffs, Haezreena said restraints should neither be imposed automatically on every arrested person nor waived simply because a suspect was prominent.
She said factors such as the risk of escape, violence, previous resistance and potential danger to the suspect or others should instead determine whether restraints were necessary.
"I don't think security and dignity are incompatible. MACC obviously has to maintain custody and ensure that someone doesn't escape or pose a danger," she said.

Title: Hadi claims Pas leaders were offered foreign help to topple government
Article:
KOTA BARU: Pas president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang has claimed that a representative of the United States (US) Embassy once asked him about the party's proposed candidate for prime minister during a meeting at the US Embassy in Malaysia.
Hadi said the question was raised after two senior Pas leaders, Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan and Datuk Dr Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar, had earlier met the US ambassador.
"He asked, 'Who does Pas propose as prime minister?' I said, 'Who does America (United States) agree with?'
"The meeting took place when Pas was still part of the Pakatan Rakyat coalition, during the visit of US President Barack Obama to Malaysia," he said.
He said this during his winding-up speech at the 72nd Pas Annual Muktamar here yesterday.
Hadi said Takiyuddin and Samsuri, who was then his political chief, had gone to the US Embassy to meet the ambassador after the meeting was arranged.
He further claimed that during the meeting, the two Pas leaders were informed of the possibility of bringing down the government and taking over the administration.
Hadi also alleged that the US was prepared to assist in the effort.
"However, Takiyuddin and Samsuri remained steadfast and were not influenced by the offer. Both our men remained steadfast. They were not influenced," he said.
Hadi said following the meeting, the US ambassador requested to meet him, and he attended the meeting with Datuk Mustafa Ali.
He said the question of a potential prime minister was also raised during the meeting, but he did not regard it as a priority as a decision would only need to be made when the time came.
"At that time, the Americans asked who the candidate they supported was, and the name of Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad was mentioned and received a positive response from them.
"I told them Mahathir. Mahathir? 'That's good,' he replied. Why fuss over who it would be? When the time comes, there will be someone. What is important is that we do our work.
"This is what is important. We resolve the divisions, resolve the crisis. Go back and work, go back and carry out our duties," he said.
Meanwhile, Takiyuddin, speaking to reporters after the muktamar, confirmed that he and other Pas leaders had met representatives of the US Embassy as referred to by Hadi.
However, Takiyuddin's confirmation did not cover all of Hadi's claims regarding the contents of the meeting.
Takiyuddin said the embassy representative had asked whether Pas, at the time, had any plans to bring down the Barisan Nasional government.
He said Pas did not provide any decision or position on the matter.
He also stressed that Pas had never sought the intervention of any foreign country in Malaysia's political affairs, including during the BN administration.
"We do not expect intervention from foreign countries because our country's politics belong to us, and there should be no foreign interference.
"If other parties want foreign intervention to bring down (the government), that is up to them. We do not," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: How haze from Indonesian fires impacts Southeast Asia
Article:
JAKARTA: Thick smog has blanketed parts of Indonesia as the vast archipelago for weeks battles to contain fires that have burned large swathes of Borneo and Sumatra.
The hazardous smoke has led to an increase in respiratory problems, forced schools to close, and has been drifting to neighbouring countries including – Malaysia, Singapore, and the Philippines.
Here's what to know:
WHERE ARE THE FIRES?
Most of the fires are concentrated on Borneo island, home to vast tropical jungle that Indonesia shares with Brunei and Malaysia, as well as Sumatra.
So far this year, nearly 300,000 hectares of land have burned in Indonesia, according to an independent estimate from the Nusantara Atlas portal.
Indonesia saw an uptick in carbon emissions since late July, and by the end of last month the levels were comparable to previous El Nino years of 2015 and 2019, Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service (CAMS) senior scientist Mark Parrington told AFP.
"We're seeing already now... really extreme fire emissions comparable to those previous strong El Nino years, and also the extent of the smoke and the haze and the air quality impacts," Parrington said.
Fires in the archipelago have released more than 23 million metric tons of carbon emissions between August 28 and September 3, according to CAMS' Fire Emission Watch portal.
It was higher than 20.7 million metric tons of emissions from fires over the same period in 2015, which was a strong El Nino year.
WHAT CAUSES THE FIRES?
Analysts said that the El Nino weather phenomenon, which the United Nations said this week could turn out to be the strongest in four decades, has contributed to creating drier conditions in Indonesia and made it easier for fires to spread.
But slash-and-burn land-clearing practices also contributed to the damage, said David Gaveau, founder of the Nusantara Atlas.
"El Nino does not ignite fires. It creates the dry conditions that allow human-started fires to escape and become very large," he told AFP.
The fires are difficult to extinguish because many occurred on peatlands, a wetland ecosystem with layers of partially decomposed organic materials that become flammable when dry.
Between January and August this year, more than 210,000 hotspots were detected in peatland areas across the country, according to NGO Pantau Gambut.
"Peat is a naturally wet ecosystem and stores large amounts of organic material. When peat is drained, this organic material is converted into fuel," Pantau Gambut spokesman Wahyu Perdana said.
WHAT IS THE IMPACT?
More than five million people across Borneo and Sumatra are directly exposed to the health risks from haze, deputy health minister Dante Saksono Harbuwono said last month.
Over 1.4 million students were attending classes remotely, with many schools closed due to worsening air quality, an education ministry official said this week.
In Malaysia, soaring pollution levels prompted the government on Friday to declare an emergency in a region of the Sarawak state in Borneo, with nearly 650 schools closed next week.
In the Philippines, air quality was slowly returning to normal after a week of reaching "very unhealthy" and "severely unhealthy" PM 2.5 levels that saw officials shutter schools in cities and provinces citing the drifting haze.
The haze also drove air quality in Singapore's central region to an "unhealthy" level on Friday, the country's National Environment Agency data showed.

Title: Sabah losing experienced medical staff after training, says Dzulkefly
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: Sabah is losing experienced medical personnel as trained staff leave the state after completing their training, said Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad.
"The reality is that Sabah is often treated as a training ground or merely a temporary stop before personnel apply for transfers out of the state.
"This cycle of training, serving and subsequently losing experienced officers threatens the continuity of our services," he was quoted as saying in a statement after speaking at the Health Minister's Dialogue Programme at Dewan Wisma Wanita here yesterday.
Dzulkefly said only 12 medical specialists reported for duty in Sabah last year, while 57 transferred out of the state.
A similar trend was seen among pharmacy officers, with 174 reporting to Sabah while 115 applied for transfers out during the same period.
He said the latest data showed that Sabah's staffing rate stood at 88.51 per cent, leaving a shortfall of 3,557 vacancies.
At present, Sabah has 2,546 doctors, 549 specialists and 10,164 nurses serving in the state.
Dzulkefly said the government had taken decisive steps to address the issue, including establishing the Health Ministry-Public Service Department (PSD) Staffing Management Task Force in April.
This was followed by the establishment of the Health Ministry-Higher Education Ministry Joint Committee in June to comprehensively map the supply and demand for medical manpower.
He said the ministry had also completed the redevelopment and upgrading of 132 dilapidated clinics in Sabah between 2023 and 2025 under the Bitara Madani initiative, involving an allocation of RM75.5 million.
"For 2026, we are planning to implement the remaining 46 dilapidated clinics in phases," he said.
Dzulkefly said the Federal Government had allocated RM1.56 billion for 53 healthcare development projects throughout Sabah through the Malaysia Plan (RMK) and negotiations under the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63).
The allocation comprises 32 physical projects involving the construction of hospitals and clinics, and 21 non-physical projects focused on ICT digitalisation and the procurement of modern medical equipment.
On digitalisation, Dzulkefly said the ministry was driving a comprehensive healthcare digitalisation agenda through the Cloud-Based Clinic Management System (CCMS).
"In Sabah alone, the CCMS is being expanded to 36 health clinics, while 100 per cent of the 44 primary dental clinics throughout Sabah are now fully using the Dental Information System.
"Healthcare services in Sabah are also being integrated with the National Information Dissemination Centre (Nadi) ecosystem, enabling residents in rural and island communities to access virtual consultations without having to travel long distances," he said.
Also present were National Institute of Public Administration (Intan) representative Rusli Harun, Intan Sabah Regional Campus director Siti Robani Yusof and Sabah Health director Datuk Dr William Gotulis.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Smart deployment to Nepal gives hope to families
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The deployment of Malaysia's Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (Smart) to Nepal has renewed hope among families awaiting news of their missing loved ones.
Families remain hopeful that those who have been uncontactable will be found, eleven days after the disaster struck.
Jamaliah Tengku Ismail, 67, said she had not given up hope of finding her husband, Muhamad Nasir Abdul Talib, 68.
"I don't know what else to say.
"I have no answer other than to keep praying. As long as he has not been found, I will continue to hope.
"I am hoping for a miracle. Who knows what God has in store for us?
"We cannot give up until God shows us otherwise," she said when contacted today.
Earlier, the eleven-member
Smart team
departed for Nepal to join the humanitarian mission.
They are expected to remain in Nepal for seven to ten days to assist in the humanitarian mission following the floods.
The team, comprising personnel specialising in search and rescue (SAR) and drone operations, boarded the Royal Malaysian Air Force A400M aircraft with 12.4 tonnes of equipment, including rescue and detection gear, communications systems, high-capacity drones, specialised tunnel rescue equipment and vehicles.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Reintroduce GST if it is more effective than SST, says DAP MP
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A government backbencher believes that it is better for the government to reintroduce the Goods and Services Tax (GST) if it is more effective than the Sales and Services Tax (SST).
Kepong member of Parliament Lim Lip Eng made the suggestion after taking into account views that the SST should be combined with the GST to ensure a more effective taxation system.
Lim, who is also the Kuala Lumpur DAP secretary, said the government should not create a complicated hybrid tax system merely to avoid using the GST label.
"An effective taxation policy should not depend on the name given to the system. Instead, it should be designed based on how effectively it can be implemented.
"The government should be prepared to consider a well-designed GST with stronger safeguards, faster refund processes and targeted assistance for low-income groups.
"Bring back the GST with proper implementation if the tax system is more effective," he said in a statement today.
Last month, the government was reported to be open to conducting a study on the need to combine the SST with the GST to improve the country's taxation system and make it more progressive.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim was quoted as saying that the government would retain the SST as the foundation, but would not rule out adopting certain GST features deemed suitable to create a better taxation system.
Lim also urged the government to demonstrate that it could achieve the RM59.6 billion tax revenue target through the SST this year before formulating a hybrid taxation system combining the SST and GST.
He said the government should provide details on the total amount of tax refunded to businesses against the RM59.6 billion tax revenue target for this year, including how quickly the refunds were processed.
"The government should also provide details on the amount collected after refunds, as well as the sectors still facing issues of double taxation and the additional costs businesses have to bear for compliance.
"These details are not minor matters. Instead, they will determine whether the implementation of a new system will be easier, fairer and more effective than the SST," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Kafe Secangkir closes its doors after owner's tragic death
Article:
KUANTAN: Kafe Secangkir in Sungai Karang Darat here, which was run by the late Nur Atiqah Sofiya Mohd Kazwan, closed its doors yesterday and will be handed over to a new tenant.
Her brother, Muhammad Hafiz Rifqi, 33, said the decision on the new tenant would be up to the premises' owner.
"For us, everything has come to an end and the Kafe Secangkir name will no longer operate at these premises, although some have expressed their wish for us to continue the business.
"Now, it is up to the premises owner, who is also the landlord, to make the choice. The next matter is the items inside the premises and whether the new tenant is interested in buying them.
"As for other items such as plates, glasses and other equipment, many customers bought them yesterday and we greatly appreciate it," he said.
Commenting on the unexpected turnout, particularly on Kafe Secangkir's final day yesterday, Hafiz expressed his appreciation for the support shown by customers.
He said some customers arrived as early as 9.30am, reflecting their continued support for the café from the day it opened until its final day.
"I appreciate the presence, support and patience of everyone who came to the café during its operating hours, from 3pm to 9pm yesterday.
"Although all 100 slices of cake sold out early, customers still came to enjoy the drinks on the café's final day.
"With the café's operations now ended, I hope it will remain a beautiful memory for everyone who has supported Kafe Secangkir all this time," he said.
The café, which began operating in 2024, was run by Nur Atiqah Sofiya, 32, who died with her
husband, Muhammad Nazatullah Nazmi, 32, and their 4-year-old son, Muhammad Armaan Nazeef, in a crash involving 11 vehicles at KM110.3 of the East Coast Highway 1 (LPT1) near Temerloh on Aug 31.
The crash also claimed the lives of Seow Beng Wain, 55, from Shah Alam, Selangor, and an 18-year-old teenager, while the 52-year-old tanker lorry driver was seriously injured.
Media reports previously said preliminary police investigations found that the crash was believed to have been caused by a cement tanker lorry losing control before hitting several other vehicles that were moving slowly.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Thunderstorms, heavy rain expected in eight states until 6pm
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning of thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds in eight states until 6pm today.
MetMalaysia said in a statement that the weather conditions were expected in Kedah, Penang, Perak, Kelantan, Terengganu, Pahang, Sarawak and Sabah.
The affected areas are Bandar Baharu and Kulim in Kedah, Seberang Perai Selatan, Seberang Perai Tengah and Seberang Perai Utara (Penang), and Kinta, Kampar, Kerian, Selama, Larut Matang and Kuala Kangsar (Perak).
The warning also covers Gua Musang, Kuala Krai and Jeli (Kelantan), Besut (Terengganu) and Cameron Highlands (Pahang).
In Sarawak, the affected areas are Subis (Miri), Kapit and Song (Kapit), Kanowit and Selangau (Sibu) and Julau (Sarikei).
In Sabah, similar weather is expected in Sook, Pensiangan, Tenom and Sipitang (Interior), Kinabatangan and Tongod (Sandakan), and Kalabakan and Lahad Datu (Tawau). – BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Six areas in Sarawak record very unhealthy air quality as of 1pm
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Six areas in Sarawak recorded very unhealthy air quality, with Serian registering the country's highest Air Pollutant Index (API) reading of 287 as of 1pm today.
No areas recorded hazardous air quality.
Department of Environment deputy director-general (development) Azuri Azizah Saedon said the six areas were Serian (287), Kuching (267), Samarahan (242), Sri Aman (251), Samalaju (202) and Bintulu (201).
She said 25 other areas nationwide recorded unhealthy air quality, while 26 recorded moderate readings and 11 recorded good air quality.
"Among the areas recording unhealthy readings were several locations in Johor, Negri Sembilan, Melaka, Pahang, Sabah, Sarawak and Selangor.
"In Sarawak, Limbang recorded an API reading of 160, Miri (182), Mukah (188), Kapit (151), Sibu (172) and Sarikei (179)," she said in a statement.
She said the readings were recorded amid continuing dry weather conditions across parts of the southern Asean region.
"The Asean Specialised Meteorological Centre (ASMC) detected 139 hotspots in Kalimantan, 138 in Sumatra and 16 in Malaysia as of Sept 4.
"Of the Malaysian hotspots, five were detected in Sabah, nine in Sarawak and two in Terengganu.
"The ASMC also reported moderate to dense haze moving northeastwards from Kalimantan towards parts of Sarawak, Sabah and Brunei."
Moderate to dense smoke was also observed over North and East Kalimantan, as well as central and southern Sumatra, while moderate haze was reported over Singapore, southern Peninsular Malaysia and eastern Java.
ENDS
KEYWORDS: Malaysia, Malaysia News, NST, nation, haze, Sarawak, Department of Enviroment, API, air quality, Serian, very unhealthy

Title: Melaka eyes RM2,500 basic salary for workers
Article:
MELAKA: The Melaka government will study a proposal to make the state one of the earliest in Malaysia to set a basic salary of between RM2,500 and RM2,800 before submitting its recommendation to the Federal Government.
Chief Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ab Rauf Yusoh said the proposal would be assessed from all angles before being submitted to the Federal Government.
"This is to ensure that our young people have better incomes to build their future in the state," he told reporters after attending the 2026 Melaka Youth Town Hall session at the Melaka International Trade Centre (MITC), Ayer Keroh, here today.
He said the state government would also create opportunities for women who had left their careers due to various factors, particularly through new projects being developed in the state.
"I will look into it. For example, at Port of Tanjung Pelepas, women were previously given employment opportunities as container truck drivers within the port area. We will look at similar opportunities at the Inland Port in Alor Gajah. We will see if there are suitable jobs for women to move forward," he said.
On the carnival, which began yesterday and runs until tomorrow, Ab Rauf said it was among the state government's efforts to provide young people the opportunities to shape their future.
The carnival features various programmes, including Jom Heboh, a career carnival and skills carnival, as well as a Town Hall session aimed at helping young people understand the direction of the state's future development.
"They also need to seize opportunities to pursue Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET), which will certainly offer them a different future.
"This is important as Melaka's people have proven to be sought after by leading global manufacturing companies in highly specialised fields, particularly technology," he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Four held over cable thefts in Kampar and Kuala Kangsar
Article:
IPOH: Police detained four local men early yesterday morning in connection with two separate cable theft cases in Kampar and Kuala Kangsar.
Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said the first arrest in Kampar was made at about 4.30am when a Malim Nawar Police Station patrol team spotted two men, aged 42 and 46, acting suspiciously at the Muniswarar Temple in Bata Malim Nawar.
He said the inspection resulted in the seizure of two cable cutters and five rolls of cable, which Telekom Malaysia (TM) technicians later confirmed belonged to the company.
"The telephone line cable had been cut and was no longer functioning, resulting in an estimated loss of about RM1,000 to TM," he said in a statement last night.
In a separate incident in Kuala Kangsar, he said police were alerted by members of the public at about 3am to the suspicious movement of two vehicles around Taman Sri Pagi, Kati.
Mohd Alwi said, acting on the information, a team from the Criminal Investigation Division of the Kuala Kangsar District Police Headquarters arrested two men, aged 24 and 36, along Jalan Raja Chulan.
Following the arrest, he said police seized a silver Toyota Vios, a cable cutter, a cable-pulling iron, three rolls of cable, a crossbody bag, a mobile phone and several other items believed to be linked to the case.
Mohd Alwi said checks revealed that all four suspects had previous records, including for drug-related offences.
He said both cases were being investigated under Section 379 of the Penal Code, with police also probing the suspects' possible involvement in other cable theft cases in the district.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: First United Sikhs Malaysia team arrives in Nepal to aid flood victims
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The first batch of United Sikhs Malaysia volunteers has arrived in Kathmandu on a humanitarian mission to assist families affected by the Nepal floods and support efforts to locate missing Malaysians.
The five-member Team A, led by Mandeep Singh and Pravin Nagapan, will be deployed for two weeks, while other teams remain on standby for the next phase.
United Sikhs Malaysia legal director Raspreet Kaur told the New Straits Times that the team's immediate priority was to reach vulnerable families, particularly those in underserved and hard-to-access areas.
"Our immediate objective is to reach vulnerable families, particularly in underserved and difficult-to-access areas, and provide practical humanitarian assistance to protect them from further hardship," she said.
The team will distribute essential supplies and temporary shelter materials to about 300 families while coordinating with local authorities and responders.
Mosquito nets and tarpaulins worth about RM28,000 have already arrived at a gurdwara in Kathmandu, while volunteers will source ropes and other essentials before heading to the affected areas.
Raspreet said Team A would assess access routes and ground conditions before entering the affected areas, while Teams B and C would remain on standby depending on needs on the ground.
"During this initial deployment, we will also assess urgent unmet needs and determine whether a larger or longer-term humanitarian response is required," she said.
The Nepal floods, which struck the Trishuli Valley near the border with China's Tibet region on Aug 26, have left more than 1,200 people dead and destroyed over 2,500 buildings.
More than 4,750 people remain missing across Nepal and Tibet.
Of the Malaysians affected, 77 have been located and brought to Kathmandu for repatriation, while
55 remain unaccounted
for.
Meanwhile, the
Smart team
deployed to Nepal is expected to remain there for seven to 10 days as part of the humanitarian mission.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Zahid's absence at Pas Muktamar does not mean Umno will go solo in Melaka polls
Article:
KOTA BARU: A senior Pas leader said Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi's absence from the Pas Muktamar yesterday did not mean Umno intended to go solo in the Melaka election.
Pas secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan said the Umno president, who is also deputy prime minister, was unable to attend due to certain circumstances.
"It is completely untrue (that Umno intends to go solo in the Melaka polls). I can confirm this because I am directly involved.
"For the Melaka election, we will continue negotiations from time to time," he said.
He said this at a press conference held during the 72nd Pas Annual Muktamar here today.
Zahid was unable to attend the opening ceremony of the Pas Muktamar yesterday due to unavoidable circumstances.
Instead, the Umno delegation to the muktamar was led by the party's secretary-general, Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Fadhlina recounts ordeal of child abuse by caregiver, loss of another to SIDS
Article:
BUTTERWORTH: Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said her personal experiences of child abuse and loss had strengthened her commitment to improving caregiver support for working mothers.
Fadhlina said her second child was abused by a caregiver who hit the child on the legs while she was working as a lawyer with a demanding schedule.
"I felt very guilty because, as a working mother and a lawyer at that time, my work schedule was very tight.
"I had no choice but to send my child to a caregiver," she said in her speech at Himpunan Gala Pesona Kasih Madani here today.
She said the experience convinced her that caregivers must demonstrate greater commitment, have access to training opportunities and understand their responsibility towards the community.
Fadhlina, who has six children, said three of them had been placed under the care of caregivers, adding that finding suitable childcare was a major challenge for working mothers.
Her experience was compounded by the death of her fourth child from Sudden Infant Death Syndrome (SIDS), which she said left her traumatised and forced her to confront the difficult choice of whether to continue working or care for her children herself.
"I had to think about whether to continue working or stop and take care of my children," she said.
Fadhlina said support from her extended family, particularly her siblings, had helped her cope while continuing to work.
She said the experience underscored the importance of building a wider childcare ecosystem that would give working mothers confidence that their children were safe and properly cared for.
"This is how caregivers support working mothers like us, who are constantly thinking about our children's safety while we work," she added.
Fadhlina also backed efforts to expand the Kasih Madani caregiver programme, saying trained and accredited caregivers could help strengthen child protection at the community level.
She said she had conveyed the importance of the programme to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and would seek its inclusion in next year's Budget to enable more women to receive support.
Fadhlina said child protection should extend beyond childcare centres to schools, with everyone in the community sharing responsibility for safeguarding children.
"It takes a village to raise a child," she said, stressing that caregivers, schools, policymakers, parents and community organisations all had a role to play in protecting
children.
She said expanding the number of trained caregivers would also contribute to women's empowerment by allowing mothers to work with greater peace of mind.
More than 230 home-based caregivers from Penang and Kedah were recognised today at Himpunan Gala Pesona Kasih Madani, marking their progress through training and professional development aimed at strengthening the quality of early childcare in their communities.
Since its launch in August last year, Kasih Madani has reached more than 1,000 caregivers across four states: Kuala Lumpur, Perak, Kedah and Penang.
Managed by Merdeka Centre with the support of the Finance Ministry through Yayasan Sime Darby, Kasih Madani is a government-driven initiative aimed at strengthening Malaysia's childcare ecosystem by empowering and building the capacity of home-based and community caregivers.
Through programmes such as Kursus Rintis Asuhan Madani and Seminar Asuhan Madani, caregivers are equipped with the knowledge and skills to improve the quality and safety of the childcare they provide.
Around 200 participants have been selected for the Bimbingan Keterampilan Profesionalisasi Asuhan Madani Professionalisation Programme, which provides a pathway for caregivers to further develop their capabilities and professional standing.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 27 illegal snares destroyed in Selangor, Perak wildlife operation
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 27 illegal snares were destroyed during the Integrated Khazanah Operation (OBK) at several wildlife crime hotspots in forests in Selangor and Perak recently.
The enforcement patrols were conducted from Aug 11 to 25 by the Department of Wildlife and National Parks (Perhilitan), General Operations Force (GOP), Marine Police Force (PPM), Perak State Parks Corporation and Selangor Forestry Department.
Perhilitan director-general Datuk Abdul Kadir Abu Hashim said the 27 snares comprised spring traps, wire loop snares and nylon loop snares.
"The figure does not include other traps and devices that were also found during the patrols.
"The type and size of snares used generally depend on the species of wildlife being targeted.
"Spring traps are commonly used to target wild boar, while wire and nylon loop snares can be used to target larger or smaller wildlife, depending on the diameter of the wire or rope and the size of the spring mechanism used," he said in a statement today.
He said, in theory, the larger the snare and spring mechanism used, the larger the wildlife that could potentially be caught.
He said that in some cases, snares might be set to target specific species such as tigers, but could also trap other wildlife passing through the area.
"Moreover, snares are often concealed and camouflaged with their surroundings to reduce the chances of detection.
"This puts non-target species at risk of serious injury or death if they become trapped and are not freed within a short period," he said.
Abdul Kadir said cooperation between agencies through continuous patrols and targeted enforcement was among the key preventive measures to protect wildlife and their habitats from encroachment by irresponsible individuals.
He said illegal snaring not only threatened wildlife species but also affected the flora and fauna that formed part of the country's natural heritage.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 11 detained to assist probe into group attack in Ipoh
Article:
IPOH: Police have detained 11 individuals to assist in investigations into a group attack that left a victim seriously injured in Taman Pengkalan Jaya here on Tuesday (Sept 1).
Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said the 26-year-old victim was approached by five men travelling in two cars at about 10.30am, who then chased and assaulted him.
He said the victim, in an attempt to escape, jumped into Sungai Kinta but was slashed with a machete by one of the suspects, sustaining injuries to his face, hands, legs and back.
Mohd Alwi said members of the public later came to the victim's aid before taking him to hospital for treatment.
"The incident was believed to have been motivated by revenge and dissatisfaction by an organised crime group against the victim," he said in a statement last night.
Mohd Alwi said all those arrested, aged between 22 and 41, had previous criminal records involving drug offences and violent crimes.
He said they had been remanded to assist in investigations under Section 326 of the Penal Code.
Mohd Alwi also urged anyone with information on illegal activities involving organised crime groups to report it through the police operations room's official channels or at the nearest police station.
–BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: From janitor to senior lecturer: UM academic turns experience into PhD research
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: From collecting rubbish as a janitor to becoming a senior lecturer at Universiti Malaya, Dr Nurul Asmaa Akmal Md Din has turned years of hard work into an academic career.
Nurul Asmaa, 30, drew on her experience in waste management for her doctoral research.
She began working as a janitor in 2018 after completing her studies, initially taking the job because she needed an income, according to Harian Metro.
"I worked as a janitor because I needed a job that could earn me money immediately.
"I was paid daily," she said.
She said the job proved valuable rather than a setback, with her experience in waste management later forming the basis of her PhD research.
"My PhD research was on waste management, which required me to draw on my experience working in the sector and collecting data for the study," she said.
Nurul Asmaa later pursued her ambition of becoming a lecturer and is now a senior lecturer at UM.
She said her journey was driven by a belief that hard work would eventually bear fruit.
"Hard work will never betray the results.
"No matter how difficult what we are working towards may be, all the exhaustion will eventually pay off," she said.
Nurul Asmaa also credited her mother for encouraging her to pursue her studies.
