Title: Pas-Umno ummah unity must move beyond resolutions, says Tuan Ibrahim
Article:
KOTA BARU: The ummah unity between Pas and Umno, which was unanimously endorsed at the Islamist party's muktamar, must be translated into action.
Pas deputy president Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man said support for the unity would usually be tested when negotiations on seat allocations for the general election begin.
He said that at that point, any decisions reached must be upheld based on the principles of wala' and thiqah, namely loyalty to and trust in the party's decisions.
"The muktamar has unanimously approved the strengthening of ummah unity, particularly with many people talking about unity or cooperation between Pas and Umno.
"I want to remind everyone that our unanimous decision to support this will be tested by Allah after this, and usually seat negotiations will become an issue whenever there is political cooperation.
"At that point, all of us will be required to ensure that the decision we make today is upheld based on wala' and thiqah. We must understand that a grand vision needs to be completed.
"It is not merely about achieving unity in the context of unanimously approving the motion, but it must be translated into compliance with what the party has decided," he said.
He said this in his winding-up speech at the 72nd Pas Muktamar here today.
Tuan Ibrahim said the Muslim Unity Committee and Seat Negotiation Committee were among the important matters that needed attention as part of the agenda or action plan following the approval of the resolution.
Therefore, he said, the ummah unity resolution should be driven by a committee that would serve as an agent for the agenda and decisions.
"Similarly, in the context of elections, the Seat Negotiation Committee is a body appointed and decided upon by the party to look at the overall picture, not just the seats we have won.
"We will uphold the principle that seats won will remain with the party that won them, and Pas will defend the seats we have won," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Haze-linked health problems on the rise, asthma cases jump eightfold
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Asthma, bronchitis, acute respiratory tract infections (URTI) and conjunctivitis are among the health problems reported to have increased amid the haze currently blanketing the country.
Public health medicine specialist Datuk Dr Zainal Ariffin Omar said the increase was linked to inflammation of the respiratory tract caused by haze.
"Recent developments show that asthma cases have increased more than eightfold.
"URTI occurs when haze pollutants weaken the lungs' defences, making it easier for viruses and bacteria to attack.
"Conjunctivitis can also occur as haze particles directly irritate the eyes," he said.
The Health Ministry (MOH), in a statement last week, said asthma cases had increased to 1,811.
Dr Zainal said fine particles in haze could irritate the respiratory tract, making the body more susceptible to viral and bacterial infections.
"Studies have found that air pollution increases the incidence of respiratory tract infections.
"The main concerns are severe breathing difficulties and lung infections such as pneumonia," he said.
He said this could lead to increased hospital admissions, particularly among children under 5 and the elderly.
Dr Zainal said children and the elderly were among those most vulnerable to the effects of haze because their immune systems and lung functions were weaker.
"People with chronic conditions such as asthma, heart disease and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) are also at risk of developing health complications from exposure to haze.
"Pregnant women and smokers should also take precautions as they face higher health risks when exposed to air pollution," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Miti seeks Budget 2027 allocations to accelerate semiconductor industry, expand Malaysian exports
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Sept 5 — The Investment, Trade and Industry Ministry (Miti) has submitted 11 initiatives to the Finance Ministry (MOF) for consideration in Budget 2027, which will be tabled next month.
Deputy Miti Minister Sim Tze Tzin said priority would be given to efforts to accelerate the semiconductor industry as a high-growth, high-value sector capable of creating more jobs for Malaysians.
“Among them, we want to accelerate the semiconductor industry because we want to focus on high-growth, high-value sectors that can create more jobs for Malaysians.
“One of the major applications we have submitted for MOF’s consideration is for the government to invest in the semiconductor industry with a substantial allocation actively,” he told reporters after officiating the Madani Kita programme at Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan Sungai Nibong here today.
According to the Dewan Rakyat calendar, Budget 2027, themed “Malaysia Madani: Menggapai Di Langit, Mengakar di Bumi”, is scheduled to be tabled by Prime Minister and Finance Minister Anwar Ibrahim on Oct 9.
Sim, who is also Bayan Baru member of parliament, said Miti had also proposed allocations to help Malaysian companies, particularly small and medium-sized enterprises, penetrate new and previously underexplored overseas markets.
He said the ministry had also proposed programmes to encourage industries to increase their use of technology and improve their capabilities, enabling them to shift from low-value to high-value activities.
“We want to bring Malaysian goods and manufactured products to overseas markets, so we have sought allocations for the government to help our companies enter markets where our presence is still limited in Central Asia, such as Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan,” he said.
Sim said the 11 initiatives comprised new programmes and improvements proposed by Miti, while existing ongoing programmes would continue to be implemented.
“Miti hopes MOF will consider all the proposals, with emphasis on strategic investments that can support the country’s economic growth in the future,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Sarawak haze crisis prompts nationwide plea to stop open burning, shield schools and businesses
Article:
SARIKEI, Sept 5 — All parties are urged to refrain from open burning activities to prevent the haze situation in Sarawak from worsening and posing risks to public health and daily activities.
Special Select Committee on Infrastructure, Transportation and Communication chairman Datuk Yusuf Abd Wahab said all open burning activities, including the disposal of rubbish and clearing of forests through fire, must cease until the situation returns to normal.
He said precautionary measures must be stepped up following the declaration of an emergency in the Serian Division by His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, yesterday.
“I urge everyone to stop open burning for now. Please do not burn rubbish or clear forests by fire. Put these activities on hold until the haze situation improves.
“We do not want this situation to continue affecting daily business, travel and other activities. Schools and many premises have had to close, and this is certainly inconvenient for everyone,” he told reporters after officiating the Tanjung Manis Parliamentary Class B2 Driving Licence Assistance Programme here today.
Yusuf, who is also the Tanjung Manis Member of Parliament, reminded the public to wear face masks when outdoors to minimise health risks caused by the haze.
The programme, organised by the Tanjung Manis Parliamentary Service Centre in collaboration with the Road Transport Department (JPJ) Sarikei Branch, attracted 1,014 candidates from across the parliamentary constituency.
Yusuf said the programme reflected the Government’s concern in helping low-income groups, particularly those in rural areas, to obtain valid driving licences at a lower cost.
“With a valid driving licence, the B40 group can use motorcycles to earn a living and increase their income. This will help improve their socio-economic status,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Ops Vulture arrests two in Teluk Intan, police seize five ATM cards, gold jewellery
Article:
IPOH, Sept 5 — Police arrested two men yesterday over unlicensed money-lending and possession of ATM cards belonging to others, during an operation codenamed Ops Vulture in Teluk Intan.
Hilir Perak police chief ACP Chua Kok Lian said the suspects were arrested by the district’s Commercial Crime Investigation Division.
He said the first arrest was at a Maybank ATM in Teluk Intan, involving a man who was making a cash withdrawal. Two ATM cards belonging to other people and RM300 cash were found on him.
“Following leads provided by the suspect, police then conducted a raid at a money-lending premises along Jalan Ah Cheong, Teluk Intan, which led to the arrest of a second man,” he said in a statement today.
He added that a search of the premises also uncovered three ATM cards and several pieces of gold jewellery, believed to be linked to the case. The seized items were estimated at RM2,050
He added that both suspects are being held at the Hilir Perak District Police Headquarters and they have been remanded until Sept 6 to assist in the investigation.
“The case is being investigated under Sections 420 and 424 of the Penal Code,” he said.
He advised the public against handing over their ATM cards or allowing others to use them, even when enticed with rewards.
“Members of the public are cautioned against engaging in any suspicious dealings involving the use of bank accounts or ATM cards, whether their own or belonging to others.
“Misusing accounts and banking facilities for criminal activities will result in stern legal action,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Teo Nie Ching says Meta must extend Facebook, Instagram safeguards worldwide for under‑18s
Article:
KULAI, Sept 5 — The government hopes Meta will expand its safety features for Facebook and Instagram users under the age of 18 worldwide as soon as possible, including daily usage limits and restrictions on access at night.
Deputy Communications Minister Teo Nie Ching said the safety features should not be limited to users in the United States, as young people in other countries, including Malaysia, also face the risk of internet addiction.
She said the measures are in line with the government’s direction to ensure that young people, particularly those under 16, do not use social media excessively.
“These measures are very important to ensure that internet addiction can be properly addressed, and we want to ensure that when everyone has access to the internet, young people also receive the protection they need,” she told reporters today after inspecting a damaged futsal court in Taman Desa Kulai.
Teo said this when commenting on the settlement of legal action involving Meta and 47 states, the District of Columbia and several US territories over allegations that Facebook and Instagram were designed with features that could cause addiction among children and teenagers.
Under the settlement, Meta has agreed to pay up to US$17.1 billion, in addition to making several changes to Facebook and Instagram to strengthen protections for underage users.
Teo said the changes include limiting the use of both platforms to two hours a day for users under 18, as well as restricting access between midnight and 6am.
Meta will also improve age verification and reduce several features that could encourage excessive use.
“Features such as ‘infinite scroll’ and ‘auto-feed’ will be discontinued, and Meta has also pledged to hide the number of ‘likes’ for underage users.
“This is to ensure that young people do not become overly focused on chasing ‘likes’ to the extent of doing something unwise simply to make their posts go viral,” she said.
She said social media platforms in Malaysia are still being given a grace period to implement measures related to restricting usage among underage users.
“Some people have asked me why their children aged 16 and below can still use social media. This is because the platforms requested a grace period, and we are still within that period,” she said.
Teo said measures to protect young people must be implemented comprehensively by all social media platforms and not just Meta.
She said restrictions on Facebook and Instagram alone would not be sufficient if other platforms such as TikTok, YouTube and Snapchat did not take similar measures.
“I think this is the right time for all social media platforms to give this serious consideration and ensure that their platforms are safe for young people.
“These measures are very important to ensure that internet addiction can be properly addressed and that young people receive the protection they need,” she said. — Bernama

Title: Budget 2027 plan: Fadhlina pushes Kasih Madani training expansion to protect children nationwide
Article:
BUTTERWORTH, Sept 5 — Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek will propose including the Kasih Madani home childminder training programme in Budget 2027 to provide greater childcare and safety support for working mothers.
Fadhlina, who is also the Nibong Tebal MP, said expanding the initiative would allow more childminders to receive formal training, improve childcare quality, and strengthen the home childcare ecosystem.
She said the cause was close to her heart as a mother of six who faced immense challenges securing reliable childcare while working as a lawyer.
Sharing her personal experience, Fadhlina revealed that three of her children were cared for by home childminders, and her second child was subjected to physical abuse by a childminder.
“My second child was abused by a childminder who caned the child’s legs. At the time, I felt overwhelming guilt because as a working mother and lawyer with a demanding schedule, I had no choice but to rely on a childminder,” she said.
“That experience made me realise that childminders must possess both commitment and a sense of responsibility to society,” she said after officiating the Gala Pesona Kasih Madani at the PICCA@Arena Butterworth Convention Centre here today.
Also present were Merdeka Center programme director Ibrahim Suffian and Yayasan Sime Darby chief executive officer Dr Yatela Zainal Abidin.
Elaborating, Fadhlina shared another personal tragedy, namely the loss of her fourth child to Sudden Infant Death Syndrome (SIDS), which left her torn between pursuing her career and staying home to care for her children.
However, she said strong support from her extended family, including her siblings, helped ensure her children received proper care while she worked.
She stressed that child protection must not end at the childminding stage, but should extend seamlessly into formal schooling through a comprehensive policy framework.
“That is why at the Ministry of Education level, we are continuing with the Child Protection Policy in schools. Everyone shares a responsibility for child protection, from home childcare all the way to school,” she said.
Fadhlina added that granting formal recognition to childminders through Kasih Madani training was a vital step in elevating the dignity of the profession.
She said certified childminders should take pride in their work, as their role directly enabled working women to remain in the workforce and contribute to national development.
More than 1,000 childminders across four states, namely Kuala Lumpur, Perak, Kedah, and Penang, have benefited from the Kasih Madani initiative since its launch in August last year.
Managed by the Merdeka Center with support from the Ministry of Finance through Yayasan Sime Darby, Kasih Madani aligns with the Madani Government’s vision to strengthen Malaysia’s childcare ecosystem through the empowerment of home and community childminders.
The initiative equips childminders with essential skills and knowledge through courses such as the Madani Childcare Pilot Course (Karisma), the Madani Childcare Seminar (Semai), professionalisation workshops, and community outreach programmes. — Bernama

Title: Emergency remains: Uggah says Serian still under haze alert despite API improvement
Article:
KUCHING, Sept 5 — Serian remains under the haze emergency despite its Air Pollutant Index (API) reading improving from the hazardous level, with the Sarawak Disaster Management Committee (SDMC) continuing to closely monitor the situation.
SDMC chairman Datuk Amar Douglas Uggah Embas said in a statement today that the Serian air quality monitoring station recorded an API reading of 334 as at 10am, placing the area in the hazardous category.
However, the reading fell to 273 by 2pm, bringing it into the very unhealthy category.
He said SDMC would monitor the API reading over the next three days to observe any fluctuations, particularly the possibility of it rising above 500.
“The API is primarily affected by the wind direction and source of hotspots,” he said.
Uggah said the monitoring would be carried out before any recommendation was made to the Sarawak Premier and Prime Minister regarding the status of the emergency in Serian.
Yesterday, Yang di-Pertuan Agong Sultan Ibrahim consented to the declaration of an emergency in the Serian Division following worsening haze that had pushed air pollution to hazardous levels, with API readings exceeding 500.
The Prime Minister’s Office, in a statement yesterday, said the decision was made after taking into consideration the advice of Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, Sarawak Premier Datuk Patinggi Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg and relevant agencies monitoring air quality in the affected area.
Although Serian remains under the emergency, Uggah said government and private offices, as well as other workplaces in the affected area, may continue operating.
This includes industries, plantations, construction sites and quarries.
“However, they must take health precautionary measures,” he said.
Uggah said SDMC was also closely monitoring air quality, weather conditions, hotspots and haze movement across Sarawak so that appropriate action could be taken as the situation develops.
The public was advised to avoid outdoor activities, while those who could not avoid exposure outdoors were advised to wear an N95 mask or, at minimum, a three-ply mask.
Uggah also urged the public to take particular care of children, senior citizens and other vulnerable groups who may be more affected by the haze.
He said SDMC would continue to monitor the situation closely and issue further updates as necessary.
The committee would also continue working closely with relevant State and Federal agencies to manage the situation.
“The health, safety and wellbeing of the people of Sarawak remain our highest priority,” he said. — The Borneo Post

Title: Melaka to study proposal to set basic salary at RM2,500-RM2,800, says CM
Article:
MELAKA, Sept 5 — The Melaka government will study a proposal to make the state one of the earliest in Malaysia to set a basic salary of between RM2,500 and RM2,800 before submitting its recommendation to the Federal Government.
Chief Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ab Rauf Yusoh said the proposal would be assessed from all angles before being submitted to the Federal Government.
“This is to ensure that our young people have better incomes to build their future in the state,” he told reporters after attending the 2026 Melaka Youth Town Hall session at the Melaka International Trade Centre (MITC), Ayer Keroh, here today.
He said the state government would also create opportunities for women who had left their careers due to various factors, particularly through new projects being developed in the state.
“I will look into it. For example, at Port of Tanjung Pelepas, women were previously given employment opportunities as container truck drivers within the port area. We will look at similar opportunities at the Inland Port in Alor Gajah. We will see if there are suitable jobs for women to move forward,” he said.
On the carnival, which began yesterday and runs until tomorrow, Ab Rauf said it was among the state government’s efforts to provide young people the opportunities to shape their future.
The carnival features various programmes, including Jom Heboh, a career carnival and skills carnival, as well as a Town Hall session aimed at helping young people understand the direction of the state’s future development.
“They also need to seize opportunities to pursue Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET), which will certainly offer them a different future.
“This is important as Melaka’s people have proven to be sought after by leading global manufacturing companies in highly specialised fields, particularly technology,” he added. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia may see 230 million tonnes of plastic waste by 2040, with 23 million entering waterways yearly, says ministry
Article:
KUALA NERUS, Sept 5 — An estimated 230 million metric tonnes of plastic waste are projected to pollute Malaysia’s terrestrial and aquatic environments by 2040, the Ministry of Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability (NRES) has revealed.
Deputy secretary-general (Environmental Sustainability) Datuk Nor Yahati Awang pointed out that approximately 23 million tonnes of this plastic waste are discharged into waterways annually, representing a significant threat to marine ecosystems.
In response, she said NRES has formulated a range of strategies and initiatives to enhance marine waste management nationwide, including the development of a uniform monitoring framework through coastal clean-up programmes.
“These efforts include beach clean-ups, systematic data collection, and monitoring. Reliable data not only facilitates evidence-based policy formulation.
“It also fulfils our international obligations under SDG 14: Life Below Water,” she said during the closing ceremony of the 2026 National Citizen Science Programme: Monitoring and Cleanup of Marine Plastic Waste at Tanjung Gelam Beach here today.
Her address was delivered by NRES deputy secretary of Natural Resource Management Division, Azrina Mohd Said.
Also present was Universiti Malaysia Terengganu (UMT) deputy vice-chancellor (Research and Innovation) Prof Dr Muhammad Ikhwanuddin Abdullah.
Nor Yahati said this approach is also recommended by The Coordinating Body on the Seas of East Asia (COBSEA), which emphasises that beach cleanup activities should be integrated with systematic scientific monitoring, uniform waste classification, quality data collection and trend analysis over time.
She stressed that prevention and reduction efforts are vital to ensure marine ecosystems, resources, and biodiversity remain protected and resilient for future generations.
Meanwhile, Muhammad Ikhwanuddin said 165 kilogrammes of waste were collected in less than two hours by over 100 participants during today’s cleanup.
He said the joint programme involving UMT, NRES and the Geng Plastik Ija association focused on collecting and sorting marine debris such as plastics, packaging materials and fishing gear, which have the potential to impact coastal ecosystems.
The data gathered, he added, will help researchers identify the types, volume and distribution of waste along the coastline, serving as a valuable resource to support future studies, monitoring efforts and environmental management planning.
“In addition to the cleanup, participants comprising students, volunteers, and local community members were also educated on marine waste classification, the importance of reducing plastic use, and the role of communities in protecting coastal areas.
“Kampung Tanjung Gelam was chosen for today’s programme due to its significance as a recreational area and coastal ecosystem that requires ongoing monitoring and care,” he said. — Bernama

Title: MetMalaysia warns of thunderstorms and heavy rain in eight states until 6pm
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 5 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning of thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds in eight states until 6pm today.
MetMalaysia said in a statement that the weather conditions were expected in Kedah, Penang, Perak, Kelantan, Terengganu, Pahang, Sarawak and Sabah.
The affected areas are Bandar Baharu and Kulim in Kedah, Seberang Perai Selatan, Seberang Perai Tengah and Seberang Perai Utara (Penang), and Kinta, Kampar, Kerian, Selama, Larut Matang and Kuala Kangsar (Perak).
The warning also covers Gua Musang, Kuala Krai and Jeli (Kelantan), Besut (Terengganu) and Cameron Highlands (Pahang).
In Sarawak, the affected areas are Subis (Miri), Kapit and Song (Kapit), Kanowit and Selangau (Sibu) and Julau (Sarikei).
In Sabah, similar weather is expected in Sook, Pensiangan, Tenom and Sipitang (Interior), Kinabatangan and Tongod (Sandakan), and Kalabakan and Lahad Datu (Tawau). — Bernama

Title: Abdul Karim: Kuching gears up for Malaysia Day celebration expected to draw 5,000
Article:
KUCHING, Sept 5 — Approximately 5,000 people are expected to gather at the Borneo Convention Centre Kuching (BCCK) for the Malaysia Day celebration on September 16.
Sarawak Minister of Tourism, Creative Industry and Performing Arts Datuk Seri Abdul Karim Rahman Hamzah said the guest of honour for the event will be Yang Dipertua Negeri Tun Dr Wan Junaidi Tuanku Jaafar, accompanied by his wife, Toh Puan Fauziah Mohd Sanusi.
He added that Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg are also expected to attend the official ceremony, scheduled to begin at 8.15 pm.
“Among the highlights of the evening are addresses by Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor, Abang Johari and Anwar.
“There will also be a signing ceremony for the Malaysia Day Special Book and recitation of the Rukun Negara pledge,” he told reporters after chairing the Malaysia Day 2026 Main Committee meeting here today.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil, who is this year’s Malaysia Day celebration co-chairman, will attend the meeting online.
The Malaysia Day celebration will feature performances by a line-up of invited artistes, a theatrical musical, and a grand finale involving Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah and Sarawak.
Meanwhile, an exhibition in conjunction with the 2026 national-level Malaysia Day celebrations will be held from Sept 10 to 16 at Plaza Merdeka, Kuching.
In addition, two thanksgiving ceremonies have been planned, one for Muslims on Sept 15 at Masjid Jamek and another for other religions on Sept 14 at Pullman Hotel, both in Kuching. — Bernama

Title: Haze affects tourist arrivals and upcoming events in Sarawak, says state minister
Article:
KUCHING, Sept 5 — Sarawak has seen a slight drop in tourist arrivals amid the current haze, said State Tourism, Creative Industry and Performing Arts Minister Datuk Seri Abdul Karim Rahman Hamzah.
He said the decline was expected to continue until the haze situation improved.
“There’s a little bit of drop in the number of tourist arrivals lately. I foresee this thing will continue on until after the haze is over,” he told a press conference after chairing the Mesyuarat Jawatankuasa Induk dan Sidang Media bersempena dengan Sambutan Perayaan Hari Malaysia Peringkat Kebangsaan Tahun 2026 at a hotel here today.
Abdul Karim said tourists planning to visit Sarawak might change their travel plans due to the haze.
“If I’m a tourist, if I plan to come to Sarawak at this time or to Kuching, I will change my plan if I am from outside,” he said.
He added that the haze was also affecting several forthcoming events, including the Borderland Music Festival, which will take place at the Sarawak Cultural Village on September 11 and 12.
“I’m quite worried myself, but there’s nothing much we can do. We’ll just hope and pray that the haze problem will go down,” he said.
Abdul Karim also advised organisers of outdoor events to monitor the Air Pollutant Index (API) and follow guidance from the State Disaster Management Committee (SDMC). — The Borneo Post

Title: MACC detains company owner for allegedly soliciting RM30,000 to secure defence‑sector financing
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 5 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Kuala Lumpur has arrested an owner of a consulting, management and business company on suspicion of soliciting and accepting bribes of about RM30,000 in return for obtaining grants and loans under the Bumiputera entrepreneur financial financing scheme for two companies related to armaments and defence.
According to sources, the woman, in her 60s, was arrested at about 6.45pm on Thursday around Kuala Lumpur.
“Initial investigations found that the suspect committed the act in March 2025 and is suspected of soliciting and accepting bribes amounting to about RM30,000 from an owner of a company related to armaments and defence,” he said.
According to sources, a seven-day remand order until Sept 10 against the woman was issued by Magistrate Aliaa Anwar after an application was made by the MACC at the Kuala Lumpur Magistrate’s Court yesterday morning.
Meanwhile, Kuala Lumpur MACC director Mohamad Zakkuan Talib when contacted confirmed the arrest and the case is being investigated under Section 16(a) (A) of the MACC Act 2009. — Bernama

Title: Serian tops very unhealthy API readings as six Sarawak areas exceed 200
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 5 — A total of six areas in Sarawak recorded Air Pollutant Index (API) readings at very unhealthy levels as of 1pm today with Serian recording the highest reading of 287.
Deputy Director-General (Development) of the Department of Environment (DOE) Azuri Azizah Saedon said five other areas in the state that recorded very unhealthy readings were Kuching (267), Sri Aman (251), Samarahan (242), Samalaju (202) and Bintulu (201).
She said 25 areas recorded API readings at unhealthy levels involving Negeri Sembilan, Melaka, Johor, Pahang, Sabah, Labuan, Sarawak and Selangor, in addition to 26 areas recording moderate air quality status and 11 areas at good levels.
Azuri Azizah said the situation occurred amid persistent dry weather conditions in parts of the Southern Asean Region.
She said based on the report from the Asean Specialised Meteorological Centre (ASMC) yesterday, 139 hotspots were detected in Kalimantan, Sumatra (138) and Malaysia (16), of which nine were in Sarawak, Sabah (five) and Terengganu (two).
“ASMC also reported that moderate to thick haze was observed moving northeast from Kalimantan to several areas in Sarawak, Sabah and Brunei.
“Moderate to thick smoke plumes were also observed in North Kalimantan and East Kalimantan as well as central and southern Sumatra, while moderate haze was observed in Singapore, the southern part of the Peninsula and eastern Java,” he said in a statement today.
In this regard, she said the DOE continued to enhance monitoring and patrols in risky areas including forests, peatlands, landfills, agricultural and plantation areas and industrial areas that could potentially be the source of open burning.
Azuri Azizah said any source of open burning or pollution identified would be investigated and enforcement action would be taken strictly in accordance with the provisions of the law and the jurisdiction of the DOE.
The public is requested to immediately report any fire or open burning incidents to the Fire and Rescue Department via 999 or the DOE toll-free line 1-800-88-2727 to enable immediate action to be taken.
The latest API reading can be consulted through DOE’s Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) at apims.doe.gov.my website or the MyJAS application. — Bernama

Title: In Nepal for eight days, Malaysian wife presses on with search for missing special‑operations firefighter
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 5 — Hani Othman, who has been in Nepal for eight days to follow the developments in the search for her missing Special Airborne Fire and Rescue Team (PASKUB) officer husband, today joined a mission to distribute humanitarian aid to disaster victims in the country, while hoping to find any clues as to her husband.
Hani, who is currently on her way from Nuwakot to Betrawati with the local non-governmental organisations (NGO) Samundra Nepal NGO and Himalayan Leaders, said that the area they are heading to is not the last location where her husband’s vehicle was detected, but she still hopes that the journey will yield clues.
“The area of my husband’s last point is further up. It’s difficult to access. But Nuwakot is also a disaster-prone area, just located further down.
“I will distribute aid to the victims here. Let’s see, who knows, we might find some clues,” she said when contacted by Bernama.
Hani said that some of the aid items were collected earlier in Kathmandu, while the rest were donated by local NGOs.
Meanwhile, through a social media post, Hani shared that yesterday she managed to distribute aid to disaster victims around Kathmandu, including those who were recently rescued in Timure, and also met the wife of her husband’s team vehicle driver.
She said the contributions from Malaysians were channelled on behalf of her husband, Senior Fire Officer II Mohd Fakhrul Munir Mohd Isa, and eight other members of his expedition team, including Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) deputy director of the Fire and Rescue Operations Division Mohd Sani Harul.
“As long as I have known them, they are all good people. They are also generous and like to help others. May Allah ease all their search endeavours and protect them all no matter where they are.
“Set aside religious and ethnic differences for now, let’s pray for the best for all of them,” she said.
So far, Hani has not received news of any new developments regarding the fate of her husband who was reported missing in the flood tragedy in Rasuwa, Nepal on August 26.
Two days after the incident, Hani flew to Kathmandu on her own initiative to get the latest updates on the search and rescue efforts for her husband.
Mohd Fakhrul, 44, was reported missing after the four-wheel drive vehicle his group was in during an expedition to Everest Base Camp (EBC) was believed to have been affected by floods while in a valley in Rasuwa.
A total of 55 Malaysians have been reported as still unreachable following the disaster that occurred on August 26, while 77 others who were found safe in Tibet and Nepal have been brought to Kathmandu to undergo processing before returning to Malaysia.
Anadolu Agency reported that the death toll from the disaster has risen to 1,220, while 4,762 people, including 844 foreigners, are still missing. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia sends families’ DNA samples to Nepal to help identify 55 missing Malaysians, says Tok Mat
Article:
SEREMBAN, Sept 5 — All DNA samples from the next-of-kin of 55 Malaysians still unaccounted for following floods and landslides in Nepal have been obtained, said Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan.
He said the samples would be sent to Nepal for the authorities there to conduct DNA matching, a process expected to take some time given the large number of victims involved.
Mohamad said Malaysia was also prepared to send experts from the Department of Chemistry to assist the Nepalese authorities with the DNA matching process, if required.
“Many other countries will also be sending their experts to assist Nepal in identifying DNA matches for the victims, which will help expedite the process,” he told reporters after attending the Pinggiran Senawang Independence Carnival here today.
Meanwhile, he said the Nepalese government had been providing excellent cooperation to the Malaysian Embassy in Kathmandu in obtaining the latest information on Malaysians affected by the disaster.
Mohamad said the ministry received daily updates from the Chargé d’Affaires of the Malaysian Embassy in Kathmandu on the search operation and the situation on the ground, while the next-of-kin were also contacted regularly whenever there were new developments.
He said Nepal had limited the entry of foreign search and rescue (SAR) teams to avoid having too many teams on the ground, which could make it more difficult for the local authorities to coordinate the operation.
This morning, 11 officers and personnel from Special Malaysian Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (SMART) departed for Nepal to assist in SAR operations in areas affected by floods and landslides. The mission is expected to last 10 days.
A total of 55 Malaysians were reported still uncontactable following the disaster on Aug 26, while some of the 77 individuals located safe in Tibet and Nepal have since returned safely to Malaysia. The remainder are expected to return on flights arranged by their respective travel agents.
In another development, Mohamad said he would meet Thai Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow in the capital on Monday to discuss efforts to enhance security in southern Thailand, as well as bilateral issues between the two countries.
He said Malaysia had been given the honour by Thailand to serve as a facilitator in negotiations with the parties concerned to help bring about peace in the region.
He added that the meeting would also discuss the best approach to ensure that efforts to promote security and peace in southern Thailand could be effectively implemented.
Mohamad said peace in the region would benefit both countries, particularly by boosting Malaysia-Thailand border trade, which is of significant value.
He also advised Malaysians planning to visit Thailand to remain vigilant and always prioritise their safety. — Bernama

Title: Chew Jetty heritage site unaffected by blaze, Penang govt to help owners of five destroyed premises, says CM
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Sept 5 — The historic Chew Jetty here was unaffected by a fire that broke out about 20 metres away and destroyed five business premises early this morning, said Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow.
He said the state government was ready to provide assistance to the owners of the five business premises, including support for rebuilding efforts.
“This involves government land. I believe the owners of the affected premises are either tenants or Temporary Occupation Licence (TOL) holders.
“Should the owners decide to rebuild the affected premises, the state government will assist in the process,” he told reporters after visiting the fire site today, accompanied by Tanjung MP Lim Hui Ying, who is also Deputy Minister of Women, Family and Community Development.
Five business premises near the Chew Jetty area here, including a car workshop, a welding shop and a timber factory, were destroyed in a fire that broke out at 1.08am today, with no casualties reported.
Chow said the Penang Fire and Rescue Department, assisted by the Volunteer Fire Brigade, had brought the fire under control, while efforts to remove the timber stacks continued after traces of the fire were detected in the wooden structures.
Situated along George Town’s iconic waterfront, Chew Jetty is part of the Unesco World Heritage Site and has been home to generations of the Chinese community since the 19th century. — Bernama

Title: ‘If Langkawi too small’: Defence minister says LIMA may need alternative venue
Article:
KOTA TINGGI, Sept 5 — The proposal to explore an alternative venue for the Langkawi International Maritime and Aerospace Exhibition (LIMA) in the future is aimed at keeping the event competitive amid growing competition among defence exhibitions in the region.
Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said continuous improvements to LIMA, particularly in terms of venue size and facilities, were necessary, especially as more neighbouring countries were also organising similar exhibitions.
“The competition to organise such exhibitions is very, very strong. If we do not improve the facilities and expand the area, we may see fewer participants.
“Indonesia and Vietnam do it, Thailand does it as well. That’s why we have to constantly make improvements,” he told reporters after presenting the National Higher Education Fund Corporation (PTPTN) Loan Advance payment (WPP) to 172 recipients here today.
He said this when asked to comment on former Prime Minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad’s view that LIMA should remain in Langkawi, as the event had already established itself as an internationally recognised brand.
Tun Dr Mahathir was reported to have said that if the existing facilities in Langkawi could no longer accommodate the exhibition’s growing requirements, the government should explore other options to ensure international industry participation was not affected.
His remarks follow Mohamed Khaled’s earlier statement that the government would explore the possibility of holding LIMA in Melaka in the future.
Mohamed Khaled said the government should consider developments in the defence exhibition industry in neighbouring countries, which now offer more extensive facilities and exhibition space.
“If, for example, Langkawi is too small to accommodate the exhibition, then we have to look for (an alternative). Otherwise, we may see fewer participants than expected.
“That’s why I mentioned an area that can accommodate more people and make it easier for them to come,” he said.
Mohamed Khaled said Klebang in Melaka was among the locations that could be considered, but major investment would be needed to develop suitable convention and exhibition facilities.
He also cited the organisation of Defence Services Asia (DSA) at the Malaysia International Trade and Exhibition Centre (Mitec) in the federal capital, saying the venue faced space constraints, particularly for displaying large defence assets and vehicles.
He said international defence exhibitions in countries such as Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates were held in venues with large exhibition areas on a single level, in addition to open spaces for displaying various defence assets.
“In Kuala Lumpur, we had to put all the vehicles inside and there was not enough space to accommodate them.
“So, perhaps (we can consider other locations), but the parties involved need to invest in providing the necessary facilities. If we do not do this, many people may not participate in the exhibition we are organising,” he said.
Asked whether the LIMA name would be retained if the exhibition were moved to another location, Mohamed Khaled said it was still too early to decide. — Bernama

Title: Government ready to declare emergency if API exceeds 400, says Arthur Kurup
Article:
KUALA BERANG, Sept 5 — The government is ready to propose declaring an emergency for any area that records an Air Pollution Index (API) reading of more than 400, in line with the standard operating procedure for haze management in the country.
Minister of Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup said the measure could be considered if the API reading was at a very dangerous level, as happened in Serian, Sarawak which recorded a reading of more than 500, leading to the declaration of an emergency.
“If it is more than 400, it is considered very dangerous and can be considered to declare an emergency,” he told reporters after officiating the Handover Ceremony of the Madani Adoption Village and Madani Adoption School Project in 2026 at Dataran Kampung Basong, here today.
Arthur said so far only three of the 68 API monitoring stations nationwide had recorded very unhealthy readings, namely in Kuching, Samarahan and Sri Aman in Sarawak, while Serian recorded readings at a dangerous level.
He said the declaration of emergency would remain in effect until the API readings showed a drop to a safer level with safety measures to be taken during that period such as school closures and wearing face masks.
It was reported yesterday that the Yang di-Pertuan Agong Sultan Ibrahim declared an emergency in the entire Serian Division, Sarawak following the haze conditions which had reached levels of air pollution that were hazardous to the health and safety of the public.
The Prime Minister’s Office in a statement announced that the decision was made after taking into account the advice of Prime Minister, Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and Sarawak Premier, Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg, as well as relevant agencies on the level of air quality in the area.
In a related development, Arthur said the cloud seeding operation carried out yesterday in Sarawak and the northern peninsula, namely in Kedah and Perlis, showed positive results with several areas recording rain starting yesterday evening until early this morning.
He said Malaysia had also received written permission from the Indonesian Government allowing the country’s air assets to enter the republic’s airspace for the purpose of cloud seeding operations.
“We have carried out cloud seeding operations in Sarawak and sometimes for wider operations, our air assets need to cross the border to ‘shoot’ at the clouds and the wind will bring the clouds to our country,” he said.
In addition, Arthur said Malaysia had also offered assets and manpower to assist in the process of extinguishing the open fires that are currently taking place in Indonesia, but so far there has been no official request from the republic in this regard. — Bernama

Title: ‘Not just Kota Kinabalu’: MOH targets Sandakan, Tawau clusters in Sabah specialist expansion
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Sept 5 — The Ministry of Health Malaysia (MOH) will begin placing resident specialists in several hospitals in Sabah such as Kota Marudu and Beaufort as a measure to overcome the shortage of specialists in the state.
Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the effort also complements the ministry’s initiative to move specialist rotation to rural areas in Sabah.
“MOH’s three to five-year target is to bridge the expertise gap in Sabah through the empowerment of the Sandakan and Tawau Clusters to the same level as Kota Kinabalu, including cardiothoracic services,” he said in a Facebook post today.
He said Sabahans who are graduates of the MOH Training Institute are now being absorbed permanently through the autonomous authority of employment, followed by a 15 per cent SSPA salary adjustment, approval of Full Transfer Allowance for officers changing permanent status and a review of ETAP (on-call) incentives.
Apart from that, he said immediate action to upgrade staff quarters in Lahad Datu, Beaufort and Kota Marudu will also be implemented through strategic collaboration between the federal and state governments.
Dr Dzulkefly said MOH has also aggressively expanded the Hospital Services Outsourcing Programme initiative to the private sector to address congestion in public hospital lobbies and wards.
The scope, he said, would be expanded to 15 critical services including dialysis treatment, diagnostic scans and periodic surgical missions to resolve patient backlogs and drastically shorten waiting times.
“This measure is further streamlined through strategic collaboration with Hospital Universiti Malaysia Sabah (HUMS) to fully utilise every medical capacity available in Sabah,” he said.
Meanwhile, Dr Dzulkefly said 53 health development projects worth RM1.56 billion would be implemented under the 13th Malaysia Plan, in addition to RM75.5 million for the repair of 132 dilapidated clinics and an injection of RM1 billion for EMR.
“Our primary digital integration target has surpassed to 1Q2027 compared to 2045 previously, a step towards realising the vision of ‘One Individual, One Record’ by 2030,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Serian town unusually quiet amid thick haze and emergency declaration
Article:
SERIAN, Sept 5 — The usually vibrant streets of Serian town, typically bustling with weekend crowds, appeared unusually quiet today, amidst the ongoing haze and the declaration of an emergency in the area.
A Bernama check around the town found that health concerns had disrupted daily activities.
However, the Air Pollutant Index (API) readings on the Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal showed a downward trend from the hazardous levels above 500 recorded the day before.
Resident Elton Arib, 33, from nearby Kampung Engkeroh, said this weekend felt starkly different from the usual, blanketed by thick haze and the pungent smell of smoke.
“Normally, the town is full of people on weekends. But today, it’s quiet because of the haze. It’s the school holidays, but we’re not letting our kids go out.
“We’re scared it might affect their health. We’re also getting them to drink more boiled water. With schools shut next week too, my primary school kid will be looked after by his grandmother in the village.”
“In this kind of weather, even motorcyclists like me have to be very careful. We can’t ride fast because we can’t see clearly,” he told Bernama.
The hazardous haze has also taken a toll on traders, including Siti Shahrizan Lamat, 25, who said the drop in customer footfall has directly affected her family’s daily income.
“People are scared to come out because of the haze. Sales were really slow yesterday, and this shop is our only regular income.
“This morning is a bit clearer than yesterday, but the town is still much emptier than a usual weekend,” said the mother of one.
Fruit seller Sakong Lek, 63, from Kampung Serian Hilir, echoed similar sentiments, hoping for clearer skies. He said the light drizzle early this morning had brought some relief.
Yesterday, the King, His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, consented to declare an emergency across the entire Serian division, as the haze had reached levels hazardous to public health and safety.
The state of emergency has also led to the closure of 647 schools in Sarawak starting Sept 7, Monday, with lessons to continue through home-based teaching and learning.
As of 10 am today, the API reading in Serian, as reported on the Department of Environment’s APIMS portal, had dropped from yesterday’s levels, but remained in the hazardous range at 334. — Bernama

Title: Thai DPM Sihasak to undertake two‑day working visit to Malaysia from Sept 6
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 5 — Thailand’s Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs, Sihasak Phuangketkeow, is scheduled to pay a two-day working visit to Malaysia from Sunday to September 7, according to the PR Thai Government.
In its Facebook post on Friday, it noted that the visit would follow up on and advance the issues discussed by the leaders of the two countries during the Thai Prime Minister’s official visit to Malaysia on July 9 to 10.
Sihasak will be accompanied by the Director of the National Intelligence Agency and Chief of the Peace Dialogue Panel for the Southern Border Provinces, Thanat Suwannanon.
The delegation is scheduled to meet Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan to discuss border security and joint development of border areas.
“Talks will focus on infrastructure development, improved road and rail connectivity and the construction of additional sections of the border fence to prevent and suppress illegal cross-border activities.
“The cooperation is expected to enhance security and connectivity between the two countries while supporting economic development in border areas and delivering greater benefits to people on both sides,” it added. — Bernama

Title: Zambry: Malaysia Higher Education Plan 2026-2035 aims to shape students with strong values alongside academic excellence
Article:
IPOH, Sept 5 — The Malaysia Higher Education Plan (RPTM) 2026–2035 is focused on developing students who are not only academically competent but also grounded in strong values and good character.
Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir said the goal of education is not merely to produce knowledgeable and skilled graduates, but to shape better individuals who are capable of navigating a changing world and the demands of the job market.
“The purpose of education is to make us better people. If we study but our character and behaviour worsen, then we have missed the point of education,” he said in a statement issued by Universiti Pendidikan Sultan Idris (UPSI) today.
He was speaking at the “Sembang Santai Bersama Doc Zam” session, held in conjunction with the Perak Sejahtera Student Carnival 3.0 at UPSI in Tanjong Malim yesterday.
Zambry emphasised that this humanity-centric approach is essential to ensure that academic excellence goes hand in hand with the development of students’ character and personal values.
He said rapid technological change, including advances in AI, large language models and computing technology, requires the higher education system to prepare students for an increasingly evolving job landscape.
“The challenges you face today are far more immense than those we encountered in our time. That is why we must make changes to the higher education system, so that you can equip yourselves to meet them,” he said.
He added that the RPTM, which charts the next decade of higher education, also introduces greater flexibility, enabling working adults to resume their studies and take advantage of the Accreditation of Prior Experiential Learning (APEL) pathway.
On the Perak Sejahtera Student Carnival 3.0, he said the programme, which brought together 807 participants from institutions of higher learning and Form Six, is an important platform for building networks, confidence and a sense of unity among Perak’s youth.
Zambry said the participants, who came from various districts and ethnicities, embody the spirit of togetherness that must be nurtured further if Perak is to produce a competitive generation of future leaders.
Meanwhile, UPSI vice-chancellor Prof Datuk Dr Md Amin Md Taff, in the same statement, said the programme provides an opportunity for Perak students to share experiences and draw inspiration from figures with extensive experience in leadership and higher education.
“Gatherings like these are important in shaping a younger generation capable of becoming future leaders and, in turn, contributing to the nation’s development,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Workplaces in Serian may operate during haze emergency with health precautions, says SDMC
Article:
KUCHING, Sept 5 — Government, private offices and other workplaces affected by the haze emergency in Serian, including industries, plantations, construction sites and quarries may continue their operations but must take health precautionary measures.
Sarawak Deputy Premier Datuk Amar Douglas Uggah Embas, who is also state Disaster Management Committee (SDMC) chairman, said the committee is closely monitoring the haze situation across Sarawak, particularly the Air Pollutant Index (API) reading in Serian.
“SDMC is currently monitoring the API level in Serian within these three days in anticipation for any fluctuation of the API level, should it increase to a level above 500.
“This monitoring is to be done before any recommendation to be proposed to Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg and Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim on the status of emergency in Serian,” he said in a statement today.
He said the API is primarily affected by wind direction and the source of hotspots.
According to SDMC, the Serian air quality monitoring station recorded an API reading of 334 as at 10 am, which was in the hazardous category.
Uggah advised the public to avoid outdoor activities, wear an N95 or three-ply mask if outdoor exposure is unavoidable, and take particular care of children, senior citizens and those who are more vulnerable to the effects of haze.
“SDMC will continue to monitor the situation closely and provide further updates as necessary.  We will continue to work closely with all relevant state and federal agencies,” he said.
His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, has consented to the declaration of an emergency in Serian Division after the API reading exceeded 500.
The decision was made after taking into account the advice of the Prime Minister and Premier of Sarawak alongside related agencies, regarding air quality in the affected area, said the Prime Minister’s Office in a statement on Friday (September 4). — Bernama

Title: Nadma sends 11‑member SMART team to Nepal for flood and landslide SAR
Article:
SUBANG, Sept 5 — Eleven personnel and officers from the Special Malaysian Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (SMART) departed for Nepal this morning to assist search and rescue (SAR) operations in areas affected by floods and landslides.
National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) director-general Datuk Meor Ismail Meor Akim said the team is led by commander Abdul Manaf Che Isa, with the mission expected to last 10 days.
“The team has been specially formed with multi-skilled personnel covering search and rescue operations, drone operations, logistics, communications and technical support,” he told a press conference here today.
He said the team is expected to arrive in Nepal at about 11 am local time before receiving an operational briefing and being deployed to identified locations, including to assist Malaysians affected by the disaster.
“We may be deployed to the tunnel area, but that will depend on the briefing there. In this operation, we will rescue anyone who needs help, but our focus will be the area where our citizens were last reported to be,” he said.
A Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) A400M aircraft carrying the SMART team under Nadma and 12.4 tonnes of SAR equipment departed from the Subang Air Base here at 9am.
Eleven members of the Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (SMART) depart for Nepal from Subang Air Base September 5, 2026. — Bernama pic
The equipment includes rescue gear, detection devices, communications systems, high-capacity drones and specialised equipment, including tunnel rescue equipment, as well as a four-wheel-drive vehicle and a 10-tonne cargo truck.
Abdul Manaf said the team would arrive in Kathmandu before receiving a briefing from the local emergency management authorities and being deployed to the designated locations.
“Our mission is very clear: it is a humanitarian mission. We are also bringing specialised equipment to prepare for tunnel rescue operations, as well as communications, medical and health equipment,” he said.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had earlier said that the Madani Government had decided to deploy SMART to Nepal to assist in SAR operations, in addition to providing US$1 million in humanitarian aid.
A total of 55 Malaysians are still uncontactable following the disaster on Aug 26. Another 77 Malaysians, who were confirmed safe in Tibet and Nepal, have been brought to Kathmandu for processing before returning to Malaysia. — Bernama

Title: Air Kelantan: Pipe leak cuts water supply in Machang, Pasir Puteh and Kota Bharu Selatan, affecting 34,000 accounts
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Sept 5 — Production capacity at the Merbau Chondong Water Treatment Plant (WTP) in Machang has dropped by almost half following a leak in a 1,000-millimetre Glass-Fibre Reinforced Plastic (GRP) raw water pipe, said Air Kelantan Sdn Bhd (AKSB).
In a statement today, AKSB said the incident had disrupted water supply in three districts, namely Machang, parts of Pasir Puteh and Kota Bharu Selatan, affecting almost 34,000 consumer accounts.
The company said repair work began at about 11 pm yesterday and was expected to be completed within nine days.
“Water supply is expected to be restored as early as Sept 14. AKSB is also mobilising water tankers to assist affected consumers, while water operators from other states have also agreed to send tankers to the affected areas,” AKSB said.
Priority will be given to critical premises, including hospitals, dialysis centres, prisons and higher education institution hostels.
AKSB said it had notified consumers of the incident via the Infoblast system through PINTAS Careline 15777 and would continue to provide updates on the situation.
It said consumers could also obtain updates through AKSB’s official website, MyAKSB application and social media platforms, Facebook and TikTok. — Bernama

Title: PM to deliver closing address and present Agro Awards at MAHA 2026 tomorrow
Article:
SERDANG, Sept 5 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim is scheduled to officiate the closing ceremony of the Malaysia Agriculture, Horticulture and Agro-Tourism Exhibition (MAHA 2026) at the Malaysia Agro Exposition Park (MAEPS), here tomorrow.
Based on the programme, Anwar is scheduled to arrive at 10.30 am before delivering the Closing Address at Hall D2 and performing the Closing Gimmick of MAHA 2026.
The programme then continued with the Presentation of Agro Awards and the Prime Minister’s visit to the exhibition site before the ceremony ended at 12 noon.
Also scheduled to be present are the two Deputy Prime Ministers and Minister of Agriculture and Food Security Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu.
The 14th edition of MAHA is taking place for 10 days from August 28 to September 6.
MAHA is the main platform for the country’s agricultural sector that brings together industry players, government agencies, entrepreneurs, as well as research and higher education institutions to highlight innovation, technology and business opportunities in the agro-food sector. — Bernama

Title: MOH: Malaysia to lead 17th Asean Health Ministers Meeting in Kuala Lumpur from Sept 7-11
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 5 — Malaysia will chair the 17th Asean Health Ministers Meeting (AHMM), which begins September 7 in the capital, the Ministry of Health (MOH) announced.
In a Facebook post today, the ministry said the five-day meeting, running until September 11, will be held at the JW Marriott Hotel.
“This time, the focus is on building a health system that is more equitable, resilient and prepared for future challenges. Let us work together to create a healthier Asean for generations to come,” the post read.
Organised by the MOH, the conference reflects the ministry’s pivotal role as a leader in regional health diplomacy, tasked with coordinating policy directions, digital health innovation and health crisis preparedness at the Asean level.
The Ministry said it will carry out extensive information-sharing and promotional coverage, both to keep the local public informed and to demonstrate to international delegates Malaysia’s active commitment to advancing the regional health agenda.
Held biennially, the AHMM is the primary platform for Asean Health Ministers to discuss regional health issues and strengthen collaboration and coordination across the health sector.
Key outcomes of the meeting include reaching consensus on regional health priorities and finalising a Joint Statement to reinforce health cooperation among Asean member states.
Themed “Healthy Asean: Together Towards Equitable, Future-Ready Health Systems,” the 17th AHMM will feature six side events spotlighting critical health issues and agendas on the Asean stage.
These will cover lung health, rare diseases, eye care, behavioural science, medical devices and pharmaceutical research. — Bernama

Title: Public briefing on Sarawak electoral boundary review set for Sept 8 in Kuching
Article:
KUCHING, Sept 5 — Rise of Social Efforts (ROSE) will hold a briefing on the Sarawak electoral boundary review this Tuesday (September 8), giving members of the public an opportunity to hear directly from the Election Commission (EC) regarding the process.
ROSE president Geoffrey Tang said the session would feature EC commissioner Mohd Faisal Syam Abdul Hazis, who would be accompanied by EC Sarawak director Abang Noraffian Abang Ibrahim.
The briefing would be held at Pua Kumbu on Level 3 of Lot 10 Boutique Hotel, Jalan Central Timur here, set to commence promptly at 7.30pm to allow sufficient time for the question-and-answer (Q&A) session.
“Electoral boundary review is an important process that has a direct impact on how people are represented in the electoral system,” he said in a statement.
Tang said Sarawakians needed to understand not only where their electoral boundaries were located, but also how the boundaries were determined, why they were being reviewed and what rights they had to agree or object to proposed changes.
He said the session also aimed to raise public awareness that a boundary review was not merely about changing lines on a map.
“It can have implications for the number of voters in a constituency, the shape of electoral constituencies, representation of the people as well as the dynamics of future elections,” he added.
Tang said ROSE believed Sarawakians should have access to accurate and balanced information, particularly while the boundary review process was under way.
“What could be better than Sarawakians themselves hearing the briefing directly from the EC?” he said.
Tang said the session would also explain how members of the public could participate in the process, including what they needed to know if they agreed or disagreed with proposed boundary changes.
“We hope that the briefing would provide an avenue for open dialogue between the EC and Sarawakians, with particular attention given to the Q&A session.
“Participants are encouraged to raise questions concerning electoral boundaries, the objection process and their implications for elections,” he said.
The programme is open to all Sarawakians interested in understanding the implications of the electoral boundary review on the electoral system and democracy in the state.
Admission is free. — The Borneo Post

Title: Understand and follow guidelines before flying Jalur Gemilang, including AI‑generated images, says national unity minister
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 5 — Malaysians are urged to exercise greater care and always refer to the proper guidelines when installing and displaying the Jalur Gemilang.
National Unity Minister Datuk Aaron Ago Dagang said the Jalur Gemilang was a symbol of national sovereignty, dignity and unity that all Malaysians, regardless of race, religion or political affiliation, must respect.
“The national flag carries our identity, history and pride as an independent and sovereign country. Do not be afraid to fly the Jalur Gemilang, but always be aware of the proper guidelines and check them before displaying it,” he said in a Facebook post today.
Aaron said the National Unity Ministry, through the Kawasan Rukun Tetangga (KRT) and Rukun Negara Secretariat, would step up efforts to raise public awareness of the correct procedures for installing and displaying the Jalur Gemilang.
According to him, the approach was aimed not only at preventing similar mistakes from recurring, but also at fostering greater understanding and instilling a spirit of patriotism, especially among the younger generation.
Aaron said unintentional mistakes should be addressed through education and awareness, while deliberate acts of insulting or belittling the national emblem should be dealt with in accordance with the law.
He said the same principle should also apply to the use of the Jalur Gemilang on social media, including content generated by artificial intelligence (AI).
Aaron said the widespread use of AI technology could sometimes result in inaccurate images of the Jalur Gemilang, including mistakes in the number of stripes, colour arrangement or the flag’s position.
“Therefore, every user has a responsibility to check the accuracy of content before publishing or sharing it. Technology should help instil patriotism, not be an excuse for us to ignore the correct display of the national emblem,” he said.
Aaron said acts such as flying the Jalur Gemilang upside down were subject to the Emblems and Names (Prevention of Improper Use) Act 1963, under which offenders could face a fine of up to RM20,000 or imprisonment for up to three years, or both.
“Respect for the Jalur Gemilang is a shared responsibility. Let us uphold it as a symbol of unity and educate the next generation to love, respect and defend the dignity of the country,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Perak exco hopes Budget 2027 will prioritise welfare of older rural residents
Article:
IPOH, Sept 5 — The Perak state government hopes Budget 2027 will give special attention to the welfare of senior citizens in rural areas, covering housing, basic amenities, mobility as well as digital access.
State Rural Development, Plantation, Agriculture and Food Industry Committee chairman Datuk Mohd Zolkafly Harun said the attention was important with the increasing elderly population in the state, as well as the migration of young people to urban areas, which resulted in some senior citizens in rural areas, especially those living alone, to face limited access to support facilities.
“The situation is more challenging for senior citizens who live alone or still reside in dilapidated houses and have inadequate basic amenities.
“Based on the information received, residents aged 65 and above in Perak accounted for about 10.2 per cent or approximately 267,600 people in 2025,” he told Bernama.
He also drew attention to housing, stressing that serious attention was needed as there were still low-income (B40) groups in rural areas living in houses that were too dilapidated and no longer economically viable to repair.
“Hence, Perak hopes Budget 2027 can give priority to the construction of new houses and repairs of dilapidated houses, particularly through the People’s Prosperity Housing Programme (PPRS).
“Priority should be given to the rural B40 group living in houses that are too dilapidated and no longer economically viable to repair,” Mohd Zolkafly said.
The Lintang assemblyman also highlighted the importance of creating a rural economic ecosystem to open up more employment and entrepreneurship opportunities, particularly for youths.
He said rural development should not focus solely on providing basic amenities, but should also be supported by an economic ecosystem capable of offering sustainable employment opportunities and sources of income to address the migration of young people to urban areas.
“The main challenge is the migration of youths. We cannot blame them because everyone is seeking better opportunities in life, so our responsibility is to bring those economic opportunities to rural areas,” he said.
In addition, Mohd Zolkafly said strong support from the Federal Government was needed in local economic development, agro-entrepreneurship, micro-businesses, food processing industries as well as the digital economy.
Such efforts should be directed at ensuring community entrepreneurs, particularly rural youths, have skills that match industry needs, including the agri-food sector, which is increasingly dependent on technology, mechanisation and automation.
He also suggested strengthening human capital through the Skills and Career Training Programme, which offers the Malaysian Skills Certificate.
“The focus is particularly on producing skilled human capital in the agri-food, mechanisation, automation and agricultural technology sectors,” he said. — Bernama
